News.title: Baby among at least 13 killed as falling boulders crush taxi during horror landslide leaving car buried under debris
News.content:
LANDSLIDE HORROR Baby among at least 13 killed as falling boulders crush taxi during horror landslide leaving car buried under debris

A BABY was one of 13 people killed when a terrifying landslide sent massive boulders crashing down onto a taxi.

The six-month-old was travelling with 14 others in India when a massive boulder hit their car without warning mangling the vehicle before setting it alight.



The SUV was completely crushed beyond recognition as its rear was caved in when found by rescuers.

Bystanders and army personnel scrambled to fight the flames as the car burned, with only two people surviving after leaping clear before it was engulfed.



Relief teams have now reached the remote crash site and rescue operations are underway.

The tragedy struck on a treacherous section of road in the Himalayan region of Himachal Pradesh.

The passengers had been stranded overnight at a nearby village after the road shut on Thursday due to another landslide.

However moments after setting off on Friday disaster struck again as a fresh section of hillside gave way on top of the group.

Officials have confirmed the death toll.

The driver has been named locally as Bir Singh while the rest of the victims are yet to be formally identified.



A local politician has ordered officials to personally oversee the rescue operation and told authorities to give survivors the best possible treatment.

His office said he was praying for strength for the bereaved families as the search continued.

In a separate tragedy the same day, a woman died and seven more were injured when a landslide hit their car as they travelled to a temple.

The region has been battered by landslides in recent days amid continuous rainfall.

It is estimated that around 300 people die a year from landslides in India.



More than 12pc of the country is considered landslide prone.

News.title: All the UK areas that have officially declared drought – plus the 8 regions at risk
News.content:
DROUGHT has been declared in the UK for the first time this year, with six areas flagging severely dry conditions.

With hosepipe bans currently enforced by eight British water providers, even more regions are at risk of drought status.



Parts of North Wales and the Upper Severn declared drought yesterday, becoming the first recorded cases in the UK this year.

The areas have seen less than two per cent of its expected rainfall this month, last getting significant rain back on July 6.



Now, North Gwynedd, Ynys Môn (or Anglesey), South Gwynedd, Dee, Clywyd, and Upper Severn are under drought status.

Several other areas in England have been moved this week from the category “normal” to “prolonged dry weather” by the Environment Agency, as soil moisture deficits hit record levels.

The whole of southern England is now in prolonged dry weather, excluding all of Kent except the north-west of the county, alongside East Anglia, Lincolnshire, Northamptonshire and the West Midlands.

To combat conditions, 23million Brits are now under a temporary hosepipe ban in their area, introduced by eight water companies.

Yesterday, the UK’s largest water provider, Thames Water, enforced a hosepipe ban for all 10million of its drinking water customers.



Anyone caught breaking the rules could face a £1,000 fine, unless an approved exemption to use a hosepipe applies.

Britain has faced extended periods of hot and dry weather this summer, with record-breaking temperatures soaring as high as 37.3C in Suffolk last month.

No water companies in England and Wales have confirmed when the temporary hosepipe bans will end in their areas.

News.title: Banned driver who killed girl, 18, and injured her twin sister in horror crash after smashing into Mercedes jailed
News.content:
TWIN TRAGEDY Banned driver who killed girl, 18, and injured her twin sister in horror crash after smashing into Mercedes jailed

A BANNED driver who killed a teenager and injured her twin sister in a head-on smash has been jailed.

Jack Reape, 31, drove head-on into a car in a devastating crash that killed passenger Chloe Pearson, 18.



Chloe’s twin sister Abigale was a backseat passenger and suffered life threatening injuries, including internal bleeding and a fracture to her collarbone.

There were also two other passengers in the car who sustained minor injuries in the collision in Cotesbach, Leicestershire, on December 15, 2023.



The two people in the car hit by Reape – a Mercedes CLK – both suffered serious life-changing injuries which still impacts their mobility.

Reape, who was also hurt in the crash, was disqualified from driving at the time and only held an expired provisional licence.



He pleaded guilty to one count of causing death by driving while disqualified, one count of causing death by dangerous driving and three counts of causing serious injury by dangerous driving.

He was sentenced to ten years in jail at Leicester Crown Court today.

Detective Constable Charlotte Wright, the officer in the case from the SCIU, said: “This was a deeply tragic incident which has had a devastating and lasting impact on multiple people.

“Reape should never have been behind the wheel. He was disqualified from driving and held only an expired provisional licence.



“His actions resulted in the death of an 18-year-old woman who had her whole life ahead of her and left several others with serious injuries.

“Abigale not only suffered physical injuries but has also had to endure the unimaginable loss of her twin sister. Our thoughts remain with her and the rest of the family.

“This investigation has taken more than two and a half years to complete.



“Thanks to the work of specialist officers and the strength of evidence gathered, Reape pleaded guilty and spared those involved the added distress of a trial.

“I hope this case serves as a stark reminder of the devastating consequences that dangerous driving can have.

“When you get behind the wheel, you carry a responsibility not only for your own safety, but for those travelling with you and also other road users.”

In a heartbreaking tribute, Abigale said: “The most devastating thing is that I came out of this incident without my twin sister.

“I’m absolutely mortified and heartbroken that I’ve no longer got her by my side.



“Rest in peace beautiful, until we meet again.”

In a separate emotional Facebook post, she added: “Words can’t describe how much I miss you Chloe, life’s never going to be same without you.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’m heartbroken and lost knowing you’re never coming back.

“I promise to always make you proud, I love you so much.”

News.title: Monster jailed for murdering baby son by shaking him to death in ‘moment of pure violence’ after downing 8 pints of beer
News.content:
A MONSTER dad has been jailed for murdering his baby son by shaking him to death after downing eight pints of beer.

Tony Bartlett, 39, attacked four-week-old Atticus “in a moment of pure violence” after arriving home in Chard, Somerset, from a night out.



The tragic tot suffered severe internal trauma to his brain and spinal cord and died in hospital seven days later.

Bartlett has now been found jailed for murder with minimum of 18 years following a trial at Bristol Crown Court.



Jurors heard the killer dad had gone to comedy club with Atticus’ mum Evelyn Ballentyne in July 2022 for their first night out since the baby was born.

While out, Bartlett downed eight-and-a-half pints of beer before returning home where Evelyn’s parents had been looking after Atticus.



Prosecutor Charles Row KC said his “loss of temper and frustration” was “almost certainly fuelled” by the alcohol.

He added: “Mr Bartlett can’t admit to himself that when he was drunk, in a moment of pure violence, he did something that he will regret for the rest of his life.”

Evelyn told police that once her parents left, she went upstairs to take her make up off – leaving Bartlett and Atticus on the sofa.



When she returned a few minutes later, the mum heard Atticus “make two big gulps as if he was trying to breathe but couldn’t”.

Evelyn then took the baby but he had “gone all floppy” and was not breathing.

Jurors heard she started to scream, gave the baby back to Bartlett and tried to get help from the neighbours.

The mum also called emergency crews and told them there was a foamy substance and milk coming out of the baby’s nose.

She said: “My baby’s not breathing, can you please come.



“He’s not breathing, he’s four weeks old, please hurry.”

A medical expert said Atticus’ injuries were consistent with those usually sustained in “high speed traffic accidents or falling from a multi storey building”.

Paediatric neurosurgeon Amedeo Calisto found he suffered a “significant head trauma” where veins at the top of the head had been “stretched and broken”.

He told jurors that no “natural cause would have caused this” and “normal or rough handling of children” would not have resulted in Atticus’ injuries.

Evelyn was originally arrested but was not charged with any criminal offence and gave evidence at Bartlett’s trial.



The dad claimed he gave Atticus a bottle but he wouldn’t drink it.

He also said he was “rubbing and patting” Atticus and bouncing him on his knee but thought he was gassy.

Bartlett said a few moments later he released some gas and made a gulping sound “almost like it was his last breath”.

When asked by officers if he caused the injuries, he said: “I don’t think so, no. I didn’t shake him”

Detective Superintendent Lorett Spierenburg said: “This is a devastating case in which a very young baby has lost his life as the direct result of a violent and cruel act.



“The loss of Atticus has had a profound effect on all those who loved him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Tony Bartlett was alone with Atticus when he suffered these catastrophic injuries and the medical evidence gathered during the investigation proves he was solely responsible for causing them, despite his claims of innocence.

“Our thoughts are very much with Atticus’s family who’ve had to endure a lengthy and complex police investigation, followed by a trial. They’ve shown great dignity and courage throughout.”

News.title: Overjoyed mum welcomes twins on her OWN birthday in rare birth – as she hails her ‘special’ babies
News.content:
A MUM is celebrating her birthday with a twist – as her twins turn one on the very same day.

Satvinder Reena Kaur welcomed her baby boy and girl on August 10 last year – exactly 32 years after she was born.



The Nottingham mum-of-three was over the moon to find out she was having twins on Christmas Day 2024.

Fraternal twins Rishi and Risha were delivered via an emergency c-section that unexpectedly delayed Satvinder’s due date by one day – miraculously falling on her birthday.



The extremely rare coincidence – giving birth to twins on your birthday – is believed to occur just 1 in 133,000 times.

Satvinder says she was in “excruciating pain” due to complications with Risha’s positioning in her womb.



She told The Sun: “I was basically ready, but Risha decided she wanted to put her hands first rather than her head, so they had to do a c-section.

“We really wanted a baby. We both burst into tears when doctors gave us the good news.

“So when I found out on Christmas day that I was pregnant, we welcomed it as a gift. It was so special. We couldn’t be happier. They are a blessing.”

Risha is three minutes older than her brother Rishi.



In another sweet coincidence care home receptionist Satvinder, who is set to return to work in September, gave birth in the same hospital where she was born.

They are the second and third additions to her family with husband Ricki Singh Bhattie, 37, – with Satvinder’s first born Anjali, 12, delighted when she became a big sister.

She says her first born Anjali, 12, was left slack-jawed when Satvinder revealed she was having twins over a FaceTime call.

“She was at a school disco and they don’t let kids into the room anymore so she was the first person I rang with the news. You should have seen her face – she had her hands over her mouth in shock.”



The East Midlands family are kicking off celebrations at an Indian restaurant with 50 family members set to join – complete with a Mickey Mouse theme and a DJ.

Satvinder said: “We are getting ready to celebrate their first birthday, and my 33th, so it’s going to be a beautiful party. We got the big parties out of the way last year.”

“It’s changed my entire concept of my birthday – I’ll have to get used to it and prioritise the twins’ big day instead!”

News.title: Syrian refugee ‘invited’ asylum seeker pal to help rape girl, 18, they met in nightclub – as both fiends are jailed
News.content:
VILE ATTACK Syrian refugee ‘invited’ asylum seeker pal to help rape girl, 18, they met in nightclub – as both fiends are jailed

A SYRIAN refugee who “invited” his asylum seeker pal to help rape an 18-year-old girl has been jailed.

Dilgash Adil, 32, plied the victim with drink until she was “falling down” drunk after meeting her in a nightclub.

He had lured her back to his accommodation in a house of multiple occupancy (HMO) in Winsford, Cheshire, where he assaulted her.

Adil then invited his friend, asylum seeker, Diyar Mohammed Abdulsalm, 28, to also rape the teenager.





Both men have now been jailed for 11 years each after being found guilty of rape.

The vile predators must also sign the sex offender register indefinitely.

Chester Crown Court heard former shepherd Adil was granted refugee status after coming to the UK in 2020 from Syria.

Abdulsalm claimed asylum in the UK in May 2023 but his immigration status still under assessment at the time of the offences.

Judge Simon Berkson told the defendants, through a Kurdish interpreter: “It is quite clear you both took advantage of her vulnerable state.

“She was frankly in no fit state to consent to anything, in and out of consciousness.

“She was targeted, in my judgment, due to her vulnerability in that nightclub.”

The court heard heard Adil had been visiting his co-defendant at the HMO on December 21 when they decided to drive to a club.



At around 12.30am, they met the victim inside who had been out with her friends.

Adil bought her more drinks and she got “noticeably” more drunk with her eyes glazed, the court heard.

At the end of the night, the fiends offered a lift to her and her male friend, which they both accepted.

But when the friend got out of the car, the rapists drove off with the woman in the car and the passenger door still open.

Following the sex attack, the victim rang her mother “extremely upset” saying she did not know what had happened to her.



In a victim impact statement, the woman said she no longer feels safe, suffers panic attacks, struggles to sleep and is anxious around strangers.

Detective Chief Inspector Ian Murray of Cheshire Police, said: “Abdulsalm and Adil targeted a young woman who could not consent due to intoxication.

“Officers quickly ensured the victim was safeguarded and arrested the pair in connection with the offences.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Despite their denials, the jury found them guilty and they have now been jailed for their crimes. Although the victim will never be able to forget what happened, I hope these sentences provide her with some closure, knowing that these men are behind bars and justice has been served.

“Anyone wishing to report a sexual offence can contact Cheshire Police on 101, or by visiting the Cheshire Police website.”

News.title: Andy Burnham says opening No10 North is ‘best day of my life’  – after jetting to Manchester on government plane
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has said that opening No10 North is the “best day of my life” – after flying there on the government jet.

The PM worked from his new Manchester outpost yesterday and hailed it as the “nerve centre” for driving devolution.



Gun cops formed a perimeter around the repurposed Heron House in the city centre where the Labour leader was mayor for nine years.

Addressing staff, the married dad-of-three said: “I cannot tell you what a proud moment this is. I think this might be the best day of my life.



“I’m not joking. I know you think I am, but I’m not.

“Things are just completely coming full circle here, for me to be here with you all in the heart of Manchester this Friday morning at the end of a fairly big week is just everything to me.”



After becoming PM on Monday, Mr Burnham has unveiled a flurry of cost-of-living measures including scrapping VAT from energy bills, capping bus fares at £2 and tax breaks for pubs.

But all three have been engulfed into rows over a lack of cash to fund them leading to muddled messaging from ministers.

Mr Burnham also dismissed criticism that No10 North was a gimmick and insisted this this was the “North Pole” to counterbalance the Downing Street “South Pole”.

He also preempted concerns about the cost to taxpayers of opening the new office and transporting ministers between London and Manchester.



Mr Burnham flew from Glasgow, where he was attending the Commonwealth Games, to Manchester on the government’s charter plane, according to the Guido Fawkes blog.

Reform’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said: “It’s all very well opening No10 North, but what’s actually changing in people’s lives? Unless Burnham fixes the fundamentals it will become a gimmick the public see straight through.

“So far we’ve had three unfunded announcements in as many days. Burnham’s blagging it without a plan and it’s going to end up with him raising taxes yet again.”

Mr Burnham has vowed to treat Britain’s low-growth economy as an “emergency” on par with the financial crash.

The PM is resurrecting the National Economic Council first launched by Gordon Brown to respond to the 2008 crisis.

News.title: Shocking moment thug swings kids’ rucksack at poor Chase the puppy before kicking him in cruel attack outside home
News.content:
A THUG was caught on CCTV whacking a poor puppy with a rucksack before booting him.

Daniel Monaghan came out of his flat carrying the blue kids’ bag and then clobbered the underfed seven-month-old German Shepherd with it.



The force of the blow forced some of the contents, including a drinks bottle, to fly out.

But the 32-year-old, from Accrington, Lancashire, was more bothered about picking up what fell out the bag than for his dog’s welfare.



The poor pet, named Chase after the Paw Patrol character, just cowered in the corner, before nasty Monaghan kicked him.

A neighbour handed over the security camera footage, filmed on July 24 last year, to the RSPCA.

Monaghan was sentenced on Wednesday (July 22) at Burnley magistrates court where he was banned from keeping animals for 10 years.

He was also ordered to carry out a 12-month community order with 15 Rehabilitation Activity Requirement Days and pay costs of £200 and a £114 victim surcharge.



Monaghan admitted causing unnecessary suffering to Chase on May 20.

Chase has now be rehomed with a new “loving” family in The Wirral and has been renamed Wolfie.

Previously underfed, he has since put on 10kg in weight.



An RSPCA spokesperson said: “The footage showed Monaghan leaving his flat before turning towards Chase and swinging a rucksack which struck the dog on the top of his head, causing some of the contents to fall out.

“The puppy responded by lying down on the ground and avoiding eye contact with his owner.

“Monaghan then stood on the German Shepherd’s lead and hit Chase on the back with his left hand before using his other foot to kick and push the puppy back into a sitting position.

“As Chase moved towards the back gate Monaghan pulled him backwards, causing the dog to fall to the ground on his left side. While the puppy lay there the defendant then kicked him with force on his left hind leg.”

RSPCA Inspector Daniel Tomlinson told the court: “I observed Chase, a young German Shepherd dog, who appeared to me to be in a lean body condition.



“He was calm and friendly. I was present while the police officer explained to Monaghan that he was taking Chase into possession.”

A vet who reviewed the CCTV footage, said: “In my opinion the needs of Chase have not been met to the extent required by good practice due to the person responsible for the welfare of this animal inflicting physical abuse.

“Thereby failing to protect him from injury, pain and suffering.”

In mitigation the court was told the defendant was remorseful about what had happened and said the flat was too small for him and Chase.

The judge told him he should be ashamed of himself and described Monaghan’s behaviour as “cruel”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Speaking after sentencing Inspector Tomlinson said: “The footage of such a young dog being abused by his owner in this way was upsetting to see, and we’re grateful to everyone who assisted us in helping to bring this case to court.

“Wolfie looks the picture of health now and it’s lovely to see images of him in his new home where he’s clearly thriving and living his best life.”

News.title: Playstation down updates: Thousands of gamers frustrated as unable to connect to server
News.content:
Video game giant Sony has confirmed that all PlayStation services are 'experiencing issues' amid thousands of reports from users worldwide, including more than 6,300 in the UK on Downdetector

Playstation down updates: Thousands of gamers frustrated as unable to connect to server

Gamers around the world, including thousands in the UK, have reported issues with the PlayStation Network, with many saying they are unable to connect to the server.

Video game giant Sony has confirmed that all PlayStation services are "experiencing issues". It added that it is working to resolve the problem as soon as possible and thanked users for their patience.

More than 6,300 reports had been logged in the UK on outage-tracking website Downdetector shortly after 3pm today.

One frustrated UK user wrote on Downdetector: "Can't load any digital games at all bought or free. Can't connect to servers to verify licences, doesn't matter what i try to load i get the same message every time."

News.title: 'Entitled' couple ask minimum wage workers for romantic surprise at 7.47pm on the dot
News.content:
'Entitled' couple ask minimum wage workers for romantic surprise at 7.47pm on the dot

A minimum wage hotel worker was baffled by an "entitled" couple's "cringe" request for a romantic dinner complete with coordinated touches and a surprise that had to happen at exactly 7.47pm

View Image The hotel staff were asked to coordinate an elaborate surprise for a couple (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

A receptionist was been left baffled by an “entitled” couple’s requests to create a “movie romance” scene in the restaurant of the hotel she works at. Working with the general public in a hospitality or customer services role is not for the faint of heart. Customers can be rude and demanding, and the long hours combined with low pay can exacerbate stress and burnout.

‌



A woman named Myrto, who is currently being paid minimum wage in her job as a hotel receptionist in Greece, recently lifted the lid on one of the more outlandish requests she’s received from guests. Taking to Reddit with a post titled: “Having to put up with requests like this as a minimum wage hotel receptionist in Greece doing 10h [shifts].”

‌



Myrto shared a screengrab of an email request centred on a “special dinner” for a couple named Lucas and Lillie. The person writing on behalf of the couple thanked Myrto for the “truly wonderful” surprise “the team has prepared” then shared more requests from Lucas “to make the evening even more memorable”.

‌



According to the email, Lucas wanted Lillie to arrive at the restaurant “blindfolded” to keep the “surprise” a “complete secret until the very last moment”. The couple also wanted to be welcomed into the restaurant by a “round of applause” from staff, followed by a second round of applause when their champagne is opened.

Lucas also wants the champagne to be opened at exactly 7.47pm as this “was the exact minute” the couple “got engaged two years ago” so is a “particularly meaningful moment” for them.

After sharing the list of requests, Myrto added: “Nothing says ‘minimum wage’ like being asked to direct a surprise entrance, coordinate two rounds of applause, and uncork champagne at exactly 19:47.

‌



"The couple themselves were nice people, it’s just wild how some guests expect the staff to choreograph an entire production while we’re already juggling check-ins, calls, and a hundred other things.”

In the comments section, fellow Reddit users were keen to share their thoughts. One person said: “People trying to recreate movie romance and then realise that without the movie lighting, soundtrack and professional camera angles it actually is just awkward and cringe.”

Another said: "Having it crossing your mind? Absolutely not cringe. Asking the whole hotel/restaurant staff something like this? 100 per cent cringe. There’s so much that if [it] never left one’s mind would make the world so much better.”

‌



A third commented: “Yea that would be a ‘no’ from me - a quick reply with ‘sorry, that would just not be possible as it would disrupt the service and experience of our other guests. If you would like that for your clients, they could book a private dinner setting instead which we do not provide here sadly. Hope this helps!’ And then don’t elaborate further, just clock out and go home at end of day.”

Someone else said: “I mean, if you have a s***-ton of money to waste you can absolutely get a (higher end) restaurant/hotel to do cringey s*** like this for you.

Article continues below

"It is insane/entitled to ask a lower end place to do it, to not expect to pay a bunch more, or to make requests like this on short notice. Clearly a minimum wage hotel receptionist is not the person to expect to handle this!”

While another added: “I am also confused, what is she blindfolded for? A restaurant and a bottle of champagne?

"I assume she knows her partner is going to be there, unless he was lost at sea up until now?”

News.title: Andy Burnham given rockstar welcome to Number 10 North by Mancunian fans
News.content:
Mancunians gathered in their droves outside Heron House, home to the new No10 North, to herald the arrival of Prime Minister Andy Burnham. “Liam Gallagher, Noel Gallagher… and Andy Burnham,” said Tom Drinkwater, a 36 year old senior video editor, born down the road in Didsbury.

Waiting in the crowd, hoping to see the main man, he added: “Burnham is a Mancunian legend. “He’s been a brilliant mayor for Manchester. The rest of the country is lucky to have him now too.” Despite a heavy police presence, people came to take selfies with the building. And what a building it is.

Andy Burnham says rates cut is his way of backing venues he loved as youngster READ MORE :

Heron House is slap bang in the centre of Manchester, with entrances onto Albert and Lincoln squares. It’s a 12 minute walk from the site of the Hacienda - the club where Mr Burnham enjoyed a boogie in his youth. Also home to the spies of intelligence service GCHQ, it’s one of the most bomb proof places in the country, with state-of-the-art security built directly into its glass walls and, rumour has it, only 25% of it built above ground.

View 3 Images Tom Drinkwater says: "Burnham is a Mancunian legend." (Image: Supplied)

‌



Inside, it looks like a coffee shop in Manchester’s trendy Northern Quarter, with plywood panelling and understated grey sofas. At Christmastime, the city’s famous giant Santa will look down on Mr Burnham from its spot atop the scaffolding-clad town hall nearby.

Dr Andrew Chimenya, a senior lecturer at the University of Greater Manchester, loves the new HQ. He told The Mirror: “You couldn’t get more central. It’s an exciting space to occupy. It’s in the hubbub, shops closeby, cafes and bars even closer. Those of us who grew up with Andy in the North West are so excited, and happy to have him here. This is not about one city, or region, but about the whole country.”

View 3 Images Dr Andrew Chimenya says: "Those of us who grew up with Andy in the North West are so excited." (Image: Supplied)

Jack Leonard, a politics student from Denton, said: “If he can bring power back to the North and share it around the country it can only be a good thing. It’s an exciting moment for the North.” The throng of people outside Heron House looked more like groupies waiting for a rock star than voters supporting their new PM.

‌



Meanwhile, as the Cabinet discussed policy indoors, hip Mancunians sipped happy hour cocktails at a buzzing Slug and Lettuce right next door. And if Mr Burnham and his crew are feeling peckish, there’s a Greggs just a few steps away.

View 3 Images Teacher Rosa Ahern told the Mirror: "Change is happening here." (Image: Supplied)

“It’s impressive that someone from the north is finally in power,” rejoiced local teenager Iris Burkitt, enjoying a day out with her mum, Emma, and brother, Amyas, as they tried to catch a glimpse of the PM.

Teacher Rosa Ahern added: “For a very long time, everyone has been talking about issues in the country - why everyone is so angry and why everyone feels left behind.

‌



“Part of the reason is that everything happens in London. If you want to symbolically and realistically change people's attitude towards the government, you have to make some sort of move to bring it away from London. That is what is happening here.”

News.title: Dad who shook his weeks-old baby son to death in moment of 'pure violence' jailed for life
News.content:
Dad who shook his weeks-old baby son to death in moment of 'pure violence' jailed for life

Tony Bartlett, of Axminster in Devon, has been jailed at Bristol Crown Court after shaking his baby son Atticus at the family home in Chard

View 2 Images Baby Atticus was just four weeks old (Image: Jam Press/Avon & Somerset Police)

A father who 'lost his temper' and killed his four-week-old baby has been jailed for life after he was found guilty for murder.

‌



Tony Bartlett, 39, has today been jailed at Bristol Crown Court for life with a minimum term of 18 years for the murder of his four-week-old son Atticus on July 16, 2022. Bartlett, of Axminster in Devon, inflicted severe injuries on his baby son in a moment of "pure violence" when he shook him at the family home in Chard, Somerset, a trial at Bristol Crown Court heard.

‌



During the trial, Charles Row KC said Bartlett had been "drunk and frustrated" when he attacked his newborn son. Bartlett and his then-partner, Evelyn Ballentyne, Atticus’s mother, had gone to a pub and comedy club that evening.

‌



View 2 Images Tony Bartlett was 'enraged' by Atticus’s inability to take the bottle as well as he thought the baby should (Image: Avon and Somerset Constabulary/PA Wire)

Ms Ballentyne’s mother Rachel Donovan and her husband went to the family’s home on Darcis Row, Chard, to care for Atticus. Over the evening, Bartlett drank 8.5 pints of lager before returning home with Ms Ballentyne.

Bartlett had been feeding Atticus with a bottle and the baby was bringing up the milk, which "enraged" him. The baby suffered severe internal injuries to the brain and spinal cord when he was violently shaken by his father.

‌



Mr Justice Cavanagh told the former postman he was "very drunk" when he carried out his fatal attack on Atticus. The judge said: "I have no doubt that this terrible tragedy would not have happened if you were not so heavily intoxicated."

Judge Cavanagh added: "In your drunken state, Atticus’s inability to take the bottle as well as you thought he should enraged you. You had a sudden fit of anger. You vented that anger on your tiny baby son.

"You shook him very violently indeed, gripping him very tightly round his ribcage. This only lasted a few seconds or at most a minute or so.

‌



"Just in that brief moment, you wanted to cause Atticus serious injury. As suddenly as you began, you stopped, your anger evaporated, and then you dozed off."

Mr Row told the court that Ms Ballentyne went upstairs "for a few minutes", leaving Atticus in Bartlett's sole care. The lawyer said: "When she returned, Atticus was lying face down across the defendant’s lap.

"She said 'he’s dead, he’s not breathing'. She noted that the defendant appeared to be asleep or at least his eyes were closed.

‌



"The defendant flipped Atticus over. Atticus released two gasps and appeared to be floppy and lifeless."

Atticus was taken to Musgrove Park Hospital by emergency services before he was transferred to Bristol Royal Hospital for Children. His brain damage was so severe he did not regain consciousness or breathe for himself.

Atticus died just before midnight on July 23, 2022. Experts said the injuries suffered by Atticus were associated with "vigorous shaking", with his rib fractures caused by "gripping and squeezing" during that attack, Mr Row told the court.

‌



In a victim personal statement, Ms Ballentyne described how she had been left with "severe anxiety" following Atticus’s death. "I will never know what kind of person Atticus would have become," she said.

She continued: "I will never see him hit milestones. I will never see him go to school. I will never see him grow up and have a family of his own."

Ms Ballentyne added: "Who plans their baby’s funeral? Who goes to the chapel of rest? I had to wait 11 hours and 18 minutes for Atticus to die. It was horrendous. I was scared to go out, I was scared to stay in.

‌



"I don’t enjoy any moments because I have a dead son. It is mentally and emotionally draining all the time. It is awful."

Her mother, Mrs Donovan, told the court how she wondered what Atticus would look like now and what toys he would like to play with. "I just want one more day with Atticus," she said.

The grandmother continued: "I’m glad I had Atticus that night. He was loved and cuddled and had a lovely night with us. I just hope and pray he never knew what happened to him."

Article continues below

Representing Bartlett, Nigel Power KC said his client had previously been a "good and caring parent" to his son. "This is not a case where there is intention to kill or premeditation," Mr Power said.

News.title: Demand for Trump's son to testify over links to rape-accused Andrew and Tristan Tate
News.content:
Donald Trump’s youngest son is being requested to testify over his links with rape-accused brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate.

The call was made as pressure grows for a US congressional investigation into the misogynist influencers’ links with the President’s inner circle. Democratic congresswoman Yassamin Ansari has urged the Republican chairman of the House Oversight Committee, James Comer, to “swiftly open” an inquiry into the Tate brothers’ “coordination and extensive relationships with members of the President’s orbit, including his son, Barron Trump.”

The British brothers were arrested by US authorities in Miami on Saturday after prosecutors in Britain issued 38 new charges against them.

View 4 Images Andrew and Tristan Tate have been arrested in Miami over new UK rape charges, which they both deny. (Image: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP via A)

The Crown Prosecution Service said Andrew Tate, 39, faces seven further counts of rape, alongside charges relating to sex trafficking and indecent images of a child. Tristan Tate, 38, has been charged with offences including two counts of rape and three counts of arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation. Both men deny all allegations.

The brothers have developed close connections with figures around the Trump administration. Andrew Tate said in 2024: “I’m very close with the Trump family. I know them well,” adding that he had spoken to Barron Trump, 20, and looked forward to seeing the President to remind him that “he’s a bulletproof bada**.”

Before Trump returned to power, the Biden administration refused to allow the brothers' entry into the US.

In a letter to Mr Comer, Ms Ansari referred to a meeting in Washington last week involving the Tate brothers, their representatives and Republican Congressman Wesley Hunt. Her letter cited reports of “detailed, direct, extensive” communications between Andrew Tate and Barron Trump, “as well as the Tate brothers’ broader interactions with high-profile political figures within the president’s personal circle.”

Ms Ansari added: “No individual, regardless of wealth, political party, or access to the first family and the president, is above the law or beyond the reach of justice.” She said the committee should question Barron Trump about “his knowledge" of the Tate brothers’ alleged crimes, and establish whether he had any involvement in, or communication with, his father or administration officials over their legal proceedings.

View 4 Images The Trump family’s links to Andrew and Tristan Tate are facing fresh scrutiny amid calls for a congressional investigation (Image: Getty Images)

Just days before Trump returned to power on January 20 last year, the Tate brothers were under investigation in Romania, where they had lived. According to The New York Times, in a text message sent on January 14, Andrew Tate suggested assistance from the Trump administration was already underway.

“I had word from The Trump admin that theyre on top of things,” he wrote to someone close to him in a message seen by the paper. “Ive been told ill be free soon but Trump needs to see me in Miami.”

The following month, Romanian prosecutors were reportedly instructed from the highest levels of government to seek a compromise with the brothers. Despite concerns, they lifted the Tates’ travel restrictions in a move Romania’s prime minister believed would placate the Trump administration.

“We’re massively back,” Tate declared in a video on February 27 as he and his brother flew by private jet to Florida.

It remains unclear whether Mr Comer will launch an investigation, issue subpoenas or seek testimony from Trump's youngest child. There is no suggestion that the President’s son committed wrongdoing or played any part in official decisions connected to the Tate case.

Barron Trump, the president’s only child to his current wife, Melania, was reportedly an admirer of Andrew Tate and spoke to him on Zoom in 2024, according to The New York Times. Donald Trump Jr. is also said to have met Tate at Trump Tower in 2017, while Alina Habba, the President’s former lawyer and briefly New Jersey’s top federal prosecutor, called herself a “big fan” during a podcast appearance in January 2025.

View 4 Images Mary Trump has attacked her uncle Donald over Barron’s reported admiration for Andrew Tate. (Image: Getty Images for The Cambridge Union)

Just two days before their arrests, Andrew and Tristan Tate attended a Washington party hosted by Paolo Zampolli, a Trump administration special envoy for global partnerships. Today, Andrew Tate had posted to his account on X: “Day 6 in SHU (special housing unit) This is punitive housing for people who murder their cellmates. No commissary, no phone calls, no yard time.

“The worst possible conditions the US gov provides to terrorists and psychopaths. I am an innocent until proven guilty extradition detainee. I’m wanted by a foreign state. I am an American citizen. WHY AM I HERE?”

The White House, Trump Organisation and representatives for Ms Ansari and Mr Comer have been approached for comment.

Other senior figures in the President’s circle have expressed support for the brothers. Vice President JD Vance follows both men on X, while Donald Trump Jr previously described their detention in Romania as “absolute insanity.”

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said on Thursday that Trump had no plans to intervene in the extradition proceedings. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who would ultimately decide whether the brothers are extradited if US courts approve the move, said there was “no role” for the administration while the case remained before the courts "or maybe ever.”

Barron Trump’s reported connection to Andrew Tate has previously drawn criticism from within the President’s family. In January, Trump’s niece, Mary Trump, said: “Now, imagine what kind of... oh gosh, what’s the word? Um, disgraceful, despicable parent you would need to be in order to think it’s OK for your son to listen to and admire Andrew Tate.”

News.title: Sarah Ferguson’s ex-boyfriend and motorsport tycoon Paddy McNally dies weeks after son
News.content:
Sarah Ferguson’s ex-boyfriend and motorsport tycoon Paddy McNally dies weeks after son

Paddy McNally, who dated Sarah Ferguson before she married Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and made his fortune in Formula One, has died aged 88

View 5 Images Sarah Ferguson with motorsport tycoon, Paddy McNally (Image: Sutton Motorsports/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Motorsport tycoon Paddy McNally - a former ex-boyfriend of Sarah Ferguson - has died, just weeks after his son.

The former racing driver, who went on to make his fortune running corporate hospitality at Formula One events, died earlier this week aged 88.

The former Duchess of York dated him for several years in the early 80s before marrying ex–husband Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor - and the pair remained good friends even after they split, with Fergie once calling him the millionaire her ‘father figure’. Mr McNally’s death comes just weeks after his son Sean died suddenly in April in the Scottish Highlands.

5 View 5 Images The former Duchess with Mr McNally at the British Grand Prix (Image: Alan Davidson/Shutterstock) 5 View 5 Images Fergie previously dated Mr McNally (Image: Collect/Shutterstock)

It is reported that in his final weeks, the tycoon gave refuge to Fergie in his Swiss ski chalet after she fled the UK following the release of the Epstein files, which revealed the former Duchess had called the paedophile financier a ‘supreme friend’.

And a source told The Sun: “Paddy always looked after Sarah and at times over the past four decades she needed a lot of looking after. He never abandoned her in life and even in his final days allowed her safe sanctuary at his home in Verbier.”

Mr McNally, who was born in Kent in 1937 but grew up in Ireland, first became a motoring journalist and competed in several racing competitions before working for tobacco brand Marlboro, which was closely linked to Formula One.

View 5 Images Mr McNally with Fergie's daughters Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie at the Cartier International Polo event (Image: Alan Davidson/Shutterstock)

He then established the lucrative Allsport company, specialising in corporate hospitality at Formula One events. From this he amassed a huge fortune with a property portfolio, which included homes around the world, including Sevenhampton Place in Wiltshire, which previously belonged to James Bond creator Ian Fleming.

He married wife, Ann, in 1967 but she died in 1980. In 1982, he began a relationship with Fergie, who was 22 years his junior.

They dated for three years until their split in 1985, and shortly after she struck up a romance with the then Prince Andrew - although she and Mr McNally remained close friends up until his death.

View 5 Images Mr McNally with Bernie Ecclestone at the Monaco Grand Prix in 2011 (Image: Alan Davidson/Shutterstock)

In the Andrew Lownie book Entitled: The Rise and Fall of the House of York, the author described the ex-Duchess of York once remarking: “He taught me so much about life. Whenever I wanted advice, I turned to him because he was so worldly-wise. He seemed to have seen and done everything.”

Mr McNally eventually sold his Allsport company in 2006 for $350million and was ranked 240th on the Sunday Times Rich List last year. Paying tribute to him the FIA - governing body for motorsport - said: "The FIA is deeply saddened by the passing of Patrick Sean McNally. He worked closely with Bernie Ecclestone and played a significant role in the commercial growth of Formula 1. We thank him for his valuable contribution to the sport."

Meanwhile, Fergie has barely been seen in public since the release of the Epstein files and was last spotted at a £2,000-a-night chalet in the Alps.

The King’s former sister-in-law was tracked down to an Austrian bolt-hole after facing calls to speak to the US authorities about convicted sex offender financier Epstein after the release of millions of documents associated with him shed new light on their relationship.

Epstein has been the downfall of her ex-husband Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, who was stripped of his titles by the King because of “serious lapses of judgment” over his friendship with the late paedophile.

Article continues below

Fergie also lost her courtesy royal divorcee title and reverted to her maiden name, and recently lost the freedom of the city of York, after councillors voted unanimously to remove the honour over her links to Epstein.

News.title: UK’s sex crime capital revealed as huge surge in sexual offences recorded
News.content:
UK’s sex crime capital revealed as huge surge in sexual offences recorded

Damning new data from the Home Office shows where sex crimes are on the rise as it is announced that 217,567 offences were recorded across England and Wales last year

View 5 Images Police figures for last year have been release by the Home Office (Image: Getty Images)

Worrying new data pin-points Britain's worst sex crime hotspots - with people in some areas of the UK more than twice as likely to offend as those in others.

Sexual assaults continue to surge, shocking new statistics show, with 217,567 offences recorded across England and Wales between March 2025 and March 2026. Home Office figures detail a rise of four per cent, almost 9,000 more than what was recorded the previous year.

Stats from 2025 show that more than 15 per cent of people aged 16 years and over - almost 7.7 million - had experienced sexual assault, while 1.9 million, close to four per cent, were a victim of rape, including attempts. There are now 73,047 registered sex offenders managed by the police in the community across the UK, according to the latest government data.

The number has risen by 85 per cent over the past 15 years, since the police force level figures were first published at the end of 2010/11. At the time, there were 36,921 registered sex offenders living in England and Wales.

View 5 Images Areas Cleveland Police are in control of ranked as the nation’s worst place for sexual offences (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Daycare worker unmasked as he faces sickening 329 child abuse charges READ MORE :

One area is considerably worse that others, with a staggering 5.0 sex crimes for every 1,000 people. Cleveland Police, which cover a 230-square-mile area that includes Middlesbrough, Stockton-on-Tees, Hartlepool, and Redcar & Cleveland, recorded the highest rate of sexual offences.

That soared above the national average of 3.5, with 12,751 sexual offences - a year-on-year rise of around 10 per cent - reported.

5 View 5 Images Paul Devaney was jailed for life at Teesside Crown Court in January 5 View 5 Images Jordan Reynolds was found guity at Bradford Crown Court (Image: WEST YORKSHIRE POLICE)

In January, Paul Devaney, 42, was jailed for life at Teesside Crown Court after admitting rape, assault with intent to commit a sexual offence, false imprisonment and controlling and coercive behaviour.

West Yorkshire was confirmed as the second-worse area for the assaults, with a four per cent rise with 4.4 sex crimes per 1,000 people. One of those was Jordan Reynolds, 30, who was sentenced to 17 years at Bradford Crown Court in March for multiple rapes.

Avon and Somerset had 4.3, with Greater Manchester slightly less at 4.2. South Yorkshire and the West Midlands both had 4.0 offenders per thousand residents.

At the other end of the scale, Surrey Police reported the lowest number of sexual offences, with 2.3. London placed below the national average, with the Met Police confirming a rate of 3.1 per every 1,000 people.

A Home Office spokesperson told the Mirror: "We are deploying the full power of the state to halve violence against women and girls in a decade.

View 5 Images Greater Manchester is fourth on the Home Office list (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

"These figures are a stark reminder of the scale of the challenge, but it is encouraging that more victims and survivors are coming forward to report these crimes. We will never give up on this fight. We will do whatever it takes to make this country safe for women and girls."

The Crown Prosecution Service say it has charged more what they describe as 'rape-flagged suspects' than at any point in the last two decades, with increases in cases referred by police, charged by prosecutors and completed in the courts.

Prosecutors charged almost four in five of those cases referred by police - the highest rate on record.

Siobhan Blake, National CPS lead for Rape and Serious Sexual Offences, said yesterday: “Victims of rape and serious sexual offences deserve a criminal justice system which will use every tool at its disposal to bring offenders of these abhorrent crimes to justice.

“I hope that by seeing how many cases our prosecutors charge from cases the police pass to us gives survivors the confidence they need to seek a justice outcome.

“Those who are questioning whether to come forward, please know we will be here to listen, no matter how long has passed, and to support you if you choose this route.”

News.title: Husband pays tribute to 'amazing' wife and mum killed in freak horse riding accident
News.content:
Husband pays tribute to 'amazing' wife and mum killed in freak horse riding accident

Experienced equestrian Kerry Donoghue, 42, suffered a fall at the Penrith Horse Trials in Cumbria and could not be saved despite medics treating her at the scene

View 3 Images Kerry Donoghue and her husband Matthew (Image: Kerry Donoghue/Facebook)

The husband of a woman who tragically died in a freak horse riding accident says their family have been left "broken".

Experienced equestrian Kerry Donoghue suffered a fatal fall during the cross-country event in Penrith, Cumbria on Saturday.

The 42-year-old, from Glasgow, had been riding Carneyhaugh Rua at the Penrith Horse Trials when the horror unfolded.

Emergency medics treated the mum-of-two at the scene but she sadly succumbed to her injuries and could not be saved.

Her husband Matthew Donoghue said in an emotional tribute online that his "amazing wife" Kerry had died on Saturday, July 18, due to a "tragic horse riding accident."

He added: "No words can describe how we are feeling at the moment we are totally broken and Kerry will forever be in our thoughts and hearts.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Kerry was an experienced equestrian (Image: Kerry Donoghue/Facebook)

"If you love someone tell them you love them kiss them hug them tell them how you feel. Life for us will never be the same again. To everyone who's messaged and for all the support my family and I have received we will be eternally grateful."

The tragedy came after the former NHS nurse appeared on the Equestrian Performance Mindset podcast in May where she said she admitted she was "this close to quitting" after witnessing a horse crush another rider, reports the Daily Record.

She said: "'You're thinking to yourself, 'Goodness, is this all worth it? Do you really want to do this? Do you really want to give it a go?'."

Kerry also said she was more scared of suffering life-changing injuries rather than dying. She added: "I was really afraid of getting hurt, but hurt in a very specific way. I was afraid of how some people have had to live their lives, and the challenges that come with that."

View 3 Images Matthew has paid tribute to his 'amazing wife' (Image: Kerry Donoghue/Facebook)

Kerry continued competing and even celebrated finishing her first British Eventing Novice competition with Carneyhaugh Rua - who she nicknamed 'Roly Poly'.

A GoFundMe page launched to support Kerry's family with unexpected costs has surpassed £19,000 in donations.

Friend David Smith said: "One of my best friends lost her life in a tragic horse accident during a show. Kerry Donoghue who was so loved by her Husband Mathew, Children - Cara (13) and Josh (20) and of course the rest of her family and friends.

Article continues below

"Kerry was a passionate advanced nurse practitioner and always cared for others throughout her career. I am raising funds to help the family with this unexpected tragedy to help support them. Thank you."

To donate to Kerry's GoFundMe, visit the page here.

News.title: Southport killer Axel Rudakubana appears to be manipulating the system, families' lawyer says
News.content:
A lawyer for the families of the children murdered by Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has said his transfer from prison to a psychiatric hospital may be an attempt to "manipulate the system".

Rudakubana, 19, was given a life sentence for the murder of three children - Alice da Silva Aguiar, 9, Bebe King, 6, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, 7 - and attempted murder of eight other children and two adults.

On Thursday, he was moved from HMP Belmarsh to Broadmoor psychiatric hospital in Berkshire.

Prisoners who are considered to present a risk to staff, inmates or themselves because of mental disorders can be moved to hospital under the Mental Health Act.

Next Wednesday marks two years since Rudakubana carried out the attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on 29 July 2024.

Lawyer Chris Walker, who represents the three bereaved families, said they "don't believe the merits" of the transfer on the basis of a mental health issue and is calling for more information from ministers.

"In my mind this is a new event, this is something which occurred whilst he was at prison, and we at this stage don't believe the merits of it in terms of him because I've seen no evidence at all until today which suggests he has a significant mental health disorder," Walker told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

He added: "We do have an evil person but being evil does not mean that you're suffering with psychosis of some sort.

"We need to know is this a single event, is this a recurring event, is this him playing the system and we need those answers."

The Prison Officers' Association told the BBC that Rudakubana was transferred due to a deterioration in his mental health.

Walker added in a separate statement that the news would "devastate" the families at any time but "the fact that this has occurred as we approach the second anniversary in our view is another move by AR who would appear to be attempting, once again, to manipulate the system".

He continued: "We have been given the barest of details and whilst we are supporting the families through this we are urgently seeking a meeting with the appropriate authorities to understand the situation before commenting further."

Prior to Rudakubana's sentencing last year, his defence lawyer told the court no psychiatric evidence could suggest a mental disorder contributed to his actions.

The court also heard how Rudakubana presented as having high functioning autism and did not have any associated learning disabilities.

Stan Reiz KC added that his client had appeared to have been a "normal child" until he reached 13, adding: "However, he did make a transition from a normal, well-disciplined child to someone who was capable of committing acts of such shocking and senseless violence."

Rudakubana was deemed mentally fit to be detained, interviewed and stand trial. His late guilty plea meant his mental health was not discussed in detail in court during a trial.

He was given a 52-year prison sentence in January 2025 but the judge was unable to impose a whole life order due to Rudakubana being 17 when he carried out the attack. He will likely never be released.

News.title: 'Extremely significant' bomb in car intercepted on way to NI, Irish police say
News.content:
A car containing an "extremely significant" bomb has been intercepted in the Republic of Ireland as it was being driven across the border for an attack in Northern Ireland, gardaÃ­ (Irish police) have said.

The vehicle was stopped during an operation targeting dissident republican activities on Wednesday, but further details are just emerging. Two people were arrested.

The vehicle was stopped on the N2 near Carrickmacross, County Monaghan, at about 15:00 on Wednesday.

A woman in her 20s, who was the driver of the vehicle, was arrested on Wednesday afternoon and a man in his 40s has since been arrested.

Irish broadcaster RTÃ has reported that gardaÃ­ sources said the bomb contained a power unit, a detonator and military grade explosives.

News.title: Angela Rayner rules out rent controls in England
News.content:
Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is not looking at bringing in rent controls in England.

She told BBC Breakfast that changes made through the Renters' Rights Act, which came into effect in May, were "already having a significant impact on the market".

She added that controls which had been implemented in some areas of the UK over the past few years had not "necessarily brought rents down".

In 2023 when he was the mayor of Greater Manchester, Burnham called for freezes to private sector rents until the cost of living crisis was over.

But Rayner told the BBC on Friday: "I don't think that rent freezes, rent controls, is a way forward at the moment.

"Three years ago, Andy called for that because there was a significant crisis in the rental market.

"We implemented between then the Renters' Rights Act which is giving renters more power and control."

Temporary rent controls were introduced in Scotland in October 2022 but expired last year.

Under new legislation, ministers in Holyrood will be able to designate certain places in Scotland as rent control areas - expected to come in by 2027.

Councils will be able to cap rent increases on some properties at a maximum of 6%.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has said he wants to see rent controls brought in for all rented property in England.

Responding to Rayner's interview, he described Burnham as "continuity Starmer", posting on X: "The new prime minister talks a lot of about helping with the cost of living crisis. This is the one single measure that would help the most and save billions. All talk."

Jeremy Corbyn, who pledged to bring in rent controls during the 2019 general election when he was the Labour leader, described Rayner's announcement as "extremely disappointing".

"There is no hope of ending homelessness if we do not stand up to vested interests and take action against extortionate private rents.

"We need rent controls, and we need them now."

Sir Sadiq Khan, the mayor of London, has also long called on the government to implement a cap.

But Gareth Bacon, the Conservative's shadow housing minister, said rent controls would be "disastrous" and "intensify the damage done by Labour's agenda that has driven landlords from the market and reduced choice for renters".

"Labour are clearly divided. Burnham's pick for housing secretary has disowned a policy he himself has repeatedly backed," he said.

The term rent controls describes a range of measures a government can implement - from capping price increases to freezing them for a period of time.

Landlord groups say they may exacerbate the housing crisis by putting owners off renting out property.

The Renters' Rights Act was brought in to give more stability and security to the 11 million people who rent from private landlords.

Under the legislation, fixed-term tenancies have been banned and it is now significantly harder for landlords to evict tenants.

Rents can also only be increased once a year to the property's "open market rent".

News.title: Chris Mason: What Burnham's first week in power tells us about his agenda
News.content:
"We are on borrowed time if we don't get a move on," Angela Rayner, the former deputy prime minister who is back in the cabinet this week as housing secretary, told the BBC's Today programme on Friday.

It has been quite the week at Westminster. Sir Keir Starmer's departure as prime minister on Monday seems rather a while ago.

The fledgling Burnham administration has been seeking to find its feet and make a decent first impression at the same time, as many try to do in the first days in a job.

There has been an early pattern in these early days: an early morning nugget of news dropping from No10.

On Thursday, it was business rates in England; on Wednesday, it was bus fares in England and on Tuesday, it was a VAT cut on electricity bills.

Today, the prime minister is assembling what Rayner calls "a pride of mayors" among others for a meeting of what is known as the National Economic Council at the new No10 North in Manchester.

Andy Burnham claims his new base in Manchester represents the beginning of "the biggest rebalancing of power our country has seen, external" and he will be "bringing forward the biggest changes in the last 40 years".

His early announcements have been considerably more piecemeal than that â he says his "10 year plan for Britain" will come later in the year.

It is worth remembering there was talk from both Boris Johnson and his allies and from Sir Keir Starmer about their plans for the decade ahead â both fizzled out rather more quickly than that.

So how should we assess how much politics has changed, or not?

The early evidence - and let's be frank, it is only that given we are just a few days in - points to Andy Burnham being both more sharp and more nimble than his predecessor in setting out what he is attempting to do and trying to point to early examples of what that might look like, with the announcements of the last few days.

With the tinkering of how the government is run, like the creation of the Office of Prime Minister, and the establishment of No 10 North, he's made it clear that the arteries of power flow very much to and from him.

He hopes he can overcome the critique of Sir Keir Starmer and others, that one of the frustrations of being prime minister can be pulling levers and nothing actually happens.

News.title: Four men dead after car crashes into lamp-post
News.content:
Four men have died after a car hit a lamp-post on Merseyside, police have said.

The car left the road and crashed on Liverpool Road, Huyton, just before 02:00 BST.

The men, two aged 23, and two others, aged 24 and 26 died at the scene, Merseyside Police said.

A 27-year-old man who was a passenger inside the vehicle has been taken to hospital and is in a stable condition, the force added.

The black Seat Cupra had been travelling from Liverpool towards Knowsley before it came off the road and hit the lamp-post.

Eleven roads in the area have been closed, including Liverpool Road and East Prescot Road, from the junction of Princess Drive and Finch Lane while police carry out their investigations.

News.title: They became best friends - then discovered they were brother and sister
News.content:
Dave Green and Andrea Urmston found they instantly hit it off when their paths crossed while working in separate roles at Manchester Airport.

The two strangers got on so well they could complete each other's sentences - which made sense when they discovered the truth.

Dave was Andrea's biological brother, but had been adopted by another family when he was a baby.

"I was shaking, I was just shaking and my heart was pounding," Andrea told the BBC. "I'd finally found him. It's unbelievable."

In 2005, Dave was managing the bus station at the airport and Andrea serviced the vending machines.

Over the next two years they became firm friends, texting and phoning each other when they were not at work.

One day during a phone call, Dave told Andrea something he had never mentioned before. He was adopted and his birth name was Stuart Proudlove.

"I kind of froze and didn't speak for a minute," said Andrea.

Her maiden name was Proudlove and she had a brother who was adopted before she was born.

"It's not a very popular name and it had to be him. Other than family, I had never heard that surname anywhere else," she added.

She immediately rang her mother, Susan, to check her long-lost brother's birth date. They matched: 24 March 1966. She called Dave straight back.

"I said 'it's got to be you, it's got to be you', and I said 'I need to see you', and so I went to pick him up," Andrea said.

News.title: Chris Brown pleads guilty to affray over nightclub attack in London
News.content:
US singer Chris Brown has pleaded guilty to affray over what prosecutors called "a vicious and unprovoked attack" in a London nightclub in 2023.

Police said CCTV showed that Brown, one of the world's biggest R&B stars, hit the victim on the head with a glass bottle several times, and that the man was then chased, pushed to the floor and kicked.

The 37-year-old star had been due to face a trial on more serious charges, which he denied - assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm, and having an offensive weapon, namely a tequila bottle. However, those charges have now been dropped.

Affray, which is defined as using or threatening violence towards someone and making them fear for their safety, is punishable by up to three years in jail. Brown will be sentenced in October.

News.title: Fifty women tell BBC they were pressured into having sex with strangers
News.content:
Warning: This story contains details of sexual acts

Fifty women have told the BBC they were pressured or coerced by their partners into having sex with strangers.

They got in contact following an investigation which told the story of a woman who said she had been pressured into having sex with more than 100 people she did not know.

Many of the women who came forward said they had sex through swinging despite not wanting to, either because they feared the consequences of refusing or felt they had to keep their partners happy.

They spoke of deep, long-lasting trauma.

"I remember many nights of my partner keeping me up all night screaming at me, threatening me, and attempting to gaslight me into believing this was something I wanted," said one woman. "It was never what I wanted."

Another told us: "I felt like I had been given away. I felt used. I felt so dirty."

Most encounters were arranged via the website FabSwingers, say the women, which claims to have more than half a million UK active monthly accounts.

Six women told BBC News they had been raped by men met through the site.

One said her partner had forced her to have sex with more than 90 men through FabSwingers. On one occasion, he held her down by the ankles, she told us.

Sixteen said intimate photos of them had been uploaded to the website without their permission.

News.title: Hero swimmer helped two children during beach tragedy
News.content:
Witnesses say a heroic day-tripper managed to haul two children back to shore during an incident where a mother and daughter drowned.

Beverly Smit, 60, described the unnamed rescuer swimming out to sea three times as the tragedy unfolded in West Mersea, near Colchester, on Wednesday evening.

Shally Rahman, 41, and Samiha Rahman, 15, were trying to rescue a seven-year-old boy from the water when they got into difficulty and died.

Essex Police said the group, from Barking, east London, were all related to each other and the boy remained in hospital, fighting for his life.

Recalling the moment the "Good Samaritan" sprang into action, Smit said: "They were calling for help and the children and adults were out there.

"He swam out, I think, three times. Two of the children he brought back were not in good condition.

"It's not an easy swim when the tide's coming in - you're swimming against the tide. The water [on Wednesday] was particularly quite cold."

News.title: Dad who murdered four-week-old son jailed for 18 years
News.content:
A man who murdered his four-week-old son after drinking up to nine pints of beer on a night out has been jailed for life with a minimum term of 18 years.

Tony Bartlett returned to the family home in Chard, Somerset, on 16 July 2022 and shook baby Atticus in what the sentencing judge described as "a sudden fit of anger".

The 39-year-old caused serious injuries to his son's spinal cord and ribs, as well as brain damage so severe he never regained consciousness or the ability to breathe independently. Atticus died seven days later.

Bartlett, who was convicted after a trial at Bristol Crown Court earlier this month, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 18 years.

Warning: This story contains details which readers may find distressing.

The trial heard the former postman, from Axminster in Devon, had gone to a pub and comedy club with his then-partner Evelyn Ballentyne on the night Attitcus was fatally injured.

It was their first evening out since their son's birth.

After they returned home, Ballentyne went upstairs and left Bartlett alone to feed Atticus.

The court heard she then found Atticus looking "lifeless" when she returned, and Bartlett appeared to be asleep.

Emergency services took the baby to Musgrove Park hospital in Taunton before he was transferred to Bristol Royal Hospital for Children, where he died seven days later.

Medical experts told the court Atticus' injuries were consistent with a car crash or a fall from a height.

The newborn suffered severe internal injuries to his brain and spinal cord, as well as three rib fractures that could not be attributed to resuscitation efforts.

News.title: Heat health alerts in effect for parts of UK as rain returns for some this weekend
News.content:
Yellow heat health alerts came into effect across central and southern England on Friday morning with temperatures forecast to reach 30C (86F) in places.

The alerts, issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), cover the East and West Midlands, eastern England, London, south-east England and south-west England and are valid from 09:00 BST on Friday until 09:00 on Sunday.

The UKHSA warns that heat is expected to cause minor impacts for health and social care services, with an increased risk to life for vulnerable people.

It comes as parts of the UK prepare to see much-needed rain this weekend - although amounts are expected to be relatively small, especially in the south.

A drought was officially declared for large parts of north and mid-Wales on Thursday.

The rest of Wales, along with much of central, southern and eastern England, is in "prolonged dry weather" category - one stage below a drought - and the Sottish Environment Protection Agency said much of eastern Scotland has moved into 'water scarcity' status

Hosepipe bans are in force for millions of the customers across eastern and southern England.

News.title: Sarah Ferguson's charity formally closes down
News.content:
Sarah Ferguson's charity, Sarah's Trust, has formally wound up and is marked as "removed" on the public register of charities.

The charity said in February it would close "for the foreseeable future" days after new details emerged about the former Duchess of York's friendship with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Among more than three million documents released by the US Department of Justice (DoJ) earlier this year were emails appearing to show Ferguson was in contact with Epstein while he was in prison for soliciting sex from a minor. Being named in the documents does not indicate wrongdoing.

The BBC has contacted Ferguson's representatives for comment on the closure of her charity.

Established in 2020, Sarah's Trust was "dedicated to supporting frontline, grassroots work to address the humanitarian and environmental crisis, the hunger crisis and issues perpetuating cycles of extreme poverty", according to its website.

In February, a spokesperson for the foundation said the decision to close had come after "some months" of discussion.

The foundation did not provide further details behind its decision to close at the time.

The massive drop of files by the DoJ earlier this year suggested Ferguson had been closer to Epstein than previously thought.

In the files, Ferguson was seen praising the late sex offender in 2009 as "the brother I have always wished for".

The emails also suggest she took her daughters along for lunch with him in Miami, days after his release from prison.

Ferguson's representatives have not responded to previous requests for comment on the documents.

The former duchess has already been dropped by multiple charities over her Epstein links.

In October, she lost her duchess title when her ex-husband, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, relinquished his Duke of York title over his links with Epstein, and she was also forced to move out of his Windsor mansion, Royal Lodge, where the couple lived together, despite having divorced in 1996.

News.title: Nine men in court over historical child sexual exploitation offences
News.content:
Nine men have appeared in court charged with a total of 41 historical sexual offences, relating to eight victims who were children at the time.

The men, aged between 54 and 76, were arrested in Newport, Swansea, London, Birmingham, Lancashire, Edinburgh and the Argyll and Bute area of Scotland earlier in July.

Gwent Police initiated Operation Oak after several women reported the abuse, which took place in south Wales between 1985 and 1996.

Appearing at Newport Magistrates' Court, the defendants were told most charges were so serious that the cases would be transferred to Crown court.

The men, who are all British citizens, were granted bail. They will appear at Cardiff Crown Court on 21 August.

Operation Oak has been described by the force as a "complex and long-running investigation into group-based child sexual exploitation in south Wales".

Many of the charges relate to the rape of children.

No pleas were entered during the short hearings at Newport Magistrates' Court on Friday.

The defendants spoke only to confirm their names, dates of birth and addresses. One appeared via video-link.

News.title: Highland wildfire smoke blows into Aberdeen - 59 miles away
News.content:
Smoke from a wildfire in the Cairngorms National Park can now be seen 59 miles away in Aberdeen following a change in wind direction.

RSPB Scotland said the situation was "serious" again at its Abernethy reserve, following a "major flare-up" due to the change in conditions as the fire entered its 10th day.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said residents and businesses in the east area of Aviemore, as well as across parts of Aberdeenshire - including Inverurie, Banchory and Kintore and surrounding areas - and as far as Aberdeen city, may see or smell smoke on Friday and into the weekend.

They advised anyone affected to keep windows and doors closed.

More than 100 firefighters have been tackling the blaze which first broke out near Ryvoan Bothy, south of Nethy Bridge, last Wednesday.

Eleven fire engines, wildlife units and a command support unit are still at the scene.

Firefighters said miles-long firebreaks had helped to contain the latest break-outs on Thursday night while drones were directing crews to hot spots.

News.title: 2,000 pigeons shot with rifles at railway stations
News.content:
More than 2,000 pigeons have been shot at railway stations and depots across the UK in 16 months, the BBC has found.

Professionals with air rifles shoot the pigeons at night in an effort to prevent droppings becoming slip hazards or causing illness, but critics say the method is inhumane.

Of the stations managed by state-owned companies, York Station recorded 608 birds shot between January 2025 and April of this year - 152 of them on a single day.

The data was sourced under the Freedom of Information Act which does not apply to private companies, so it is possible other stations have culled more and the total is higher than the current figure of 2,019.

News.title: Novel analysis reveals playful side of Alan Turing
News.content:
A story written by World War Two codebreaker Alan Turing suggests he was a man with playful humour embracing his homosexuality, according to new analysis.

The six-page hand-written short story, Pryce's Buoy, has been transcribed in full for the first time and studied by Sarah Dillon, professor of literature at the University of Cambridge.

Dillon said the story offered fresh insights that challenge the view of Turing as an isolated, lonely genius.

"We've distilled a version of Turing that is a two-dimensional stereotype," she added.

Turing played a crucial role in the Allies' victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two by helping to crack codes and deciphering the infamous Enigma machine at Bletchley Park.

After the war he produced a detailed design for a digital computer in the modern sense, storing programmes in its memory.

Busted’s James Bourne given a health update after he pulled out of his latest Busted Vs McFly tour.

The 42-year-old pulled out citing health issues in September last year.

In April this year he said he had undergone “major surgery that should extend my life”.

Since then, Bourne has deleted his Instagram account and not shared any additional details.

However he has now taken to X to reveal he is “still not out of the woods yet”, adding he would reveal more soon.

“As I’m taking a break from the gram, I’ll be posting an update soon about what’s going on with my health in my Spotify bio,” he said.

“It’s a long story. Still not out of the woods yet. Thanks for your support and patience.”

open image in gallery James Bourne, Charlie Simpson and Matt Willis the band Busted attend the Rolling Stone UK Awards 2023 at The Roundhouse on November 23, 2023 in London, England ( Getty )

When announcing he had to quit the Busted Vs McFly tour, Bourne shared on Instagram: “The VS tour kicks off tomorrow night in Birmingham and as excited as I’ve been all year for this tour to begin.

“I’m really sorry to say that over the last 8 days it has become clear that I am not in good enough health to play these shows.”

“There’s a lot of information I still don’t have about my condition but my bandmates, management and I are unanimous in deciding that I should focus on the medical stuff for now.”

Although he did not go into any further details on his health issues, Bourne said his bandmates Matt Willis and Charlie Simpson supported his decision to step down.

open image in gallery ( Getty )

During the first show of the tour, Willis told fans that Bourne was “really sick”, adding: “We love him, and we miss him.”

When sharing his statement on social media, Bourne also told fans he “really hoped I can be in a position to come back further down the line”.

However he then did not post on social media for six months, but returned in April and revealed he required surgery, but did not say what for.

He posted on Instagram: “I have a plan in place to have a major surgery that should extend my life and hopefully make me well enough to come back to what I love the most which is touring and making music. It really sucks to be out of the game. But there is hope!”

Busted were formed in 2000 and have had released four studio albums, four UK number-one singles, and won two Brit Awards.
