Sports.title: Gianni Infantino accused of contempt as scale of World Cup private jet travel emerges
Sports.content:
If you took any more than a passing interest in the World Cup this summer you will have seen Gianni Infantino. Really, you couldn't miss him; the FIFA president was almost ubiquitous.

No matter where the 104 matches were being played, the bald head of the head of football's governing body seemed to be there, shining back at you out of the TV.

In fact, Infantino managed to personally attend 44 matches between the World Cup opener on June 11 and the final between Spain and Argentina on July 19. That is more than one per day, despite the World Cup being spread across 16 cities in three countries.

Logistically speaking, it is an impressive achievement, and thanks to an agreement with the Host Broadcast Service (which is 49 per cent owned by FIFA) that meant a "dignitary shot" was mandatory in every half, his efforts were rewarded with regular airtime. The 56-year-old wanted to be front and centre of the biggest World Cup of all time and, in achieving his personal goal, he was successful, visiting every host city.

‌



Infantino wanted to network. He wanted to rub shoulders with US President Donald Trump, with the governor of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund Yasir Al-Rumayyan, with countless world leaders and the heads of FIFA member associations in the posh seats.

FIFA accused of environmental negligence as extent of 2026 World Cup pollution becomes clear READ MORE :

His efforts helped firm up his control of FIFA, with the Guardian reporting that Infantino has the formal endorsement of more than 200 members for re-election as president. Even the scandal of Trump interfering with FIFA protocols to help US striker Folarin Balogun's red card be overturned couldn't diminish Infantino's standing.

Yet the method by which Infantino achieved all of this - plus a reported endorsement from Trump to become the next United Nations secretary general - casts a long shadow over the whole charade: a Qatar Airways-sponsored private jet.

Flight data shows that Infantino covered 106,323 km (66,066 miles) - almost three times the Earth's circumference - during the World Cup in a private Gulfstream G650, burning 1,020.3 tonnes of CO₂e in the process.

‌



View 4 Images Gianni Infantino used the World Cup as a networking event (Image: Eva Marie Uzcategui/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA's decision to expand the tournament to 48 teams and spread it over three countries made it the most polluting World Cup in history right off the bat, with predicted emissions of nine million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (MtCO2e), almost double the historical average from previous tournaments between 2010 and 2022. The vast majority of those emissions come from air travel.

FIFA has pledged to cut green house gas emissions 50 per cent by 2030 and reach net zero by 2040, while Infantino promised to leave a "positive footprint" on North America. Campaigners believe that his actions speak louder than his words.

“As players and supporters struggled through extreme heat, Infantino’s Qatari private jet took him from VIP box to VIP box across his bloated tournament," said Frank Huisingh, founder of Fossil Free Football. "There could be no more perfect illustration for FIFA’s wilful blindness to the climate threats facing football and its fans."

‌



View 4 Images Gianni Infantino, pictured in 2017, has regularly travelled by Qatar executive jet (Image: ISAAC KASAMANI/AFP via Getty Images)

Katie Cross, chief executive of sports sustainability charity Pledgeball, said: “The incredible emissions generated by Infantino’s private jet usage, against a backdrop of heat waves, wild fires and fans priced out of the World Cup, smack of a complete disregard for the longevity of the game, the players and the fans who make it.”

Andrew Simms, director of New Weather Institute, said Infantino's jet left behind " a cloud of contempt", while Freddie Daley, of the Cool Down Sport for Climate Action Network, noted that "it is further evidence that he and FIFA cannot be trusted to protect the game from a worsening climate crisis.”

Jenny Amann, a doctoral researcher at Loughborough University, has been interviewing fans about the relationship between climate change and football and has consistently heard negative reviews of the FIFA president.

‌



View 4 Images Gianni Infantino managed to shake a lot of hands at a huge environmental cost (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"I cannot recall a single interview in which Infantino’s actions and decision-making were not criticised," she said. "Fans consistently describe his approach as absurd and hypocritical, expressing frustration at being asked to adopt more climate-friendly behaviours while international football and its leaders continue to operate in a way that is totally detached from the broader societal crises we face.

"Infantino's travel choices at this tournament will generate emissions hundreds of times greater than the average European football fan produces in an entire year. Actions like these will do nothing to encourage fans towards more sustainable behaviours - and they suggest neither Infantino nor FIFA has any intention of leading by example.”

There is a sense of incredulity behind the scenes at FIFA at the criticism of Infantino, with the common defence being he couldn't have just watched the tournament from an office in Miami. Infantino is keen to present himself as the opposite of UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin, who was criticised last summer for only attending two matches at the Women's Euros.

‌



When asked about Infantinio's private jet usage and the environmental concerns it raised, a FIFA spokesperson said: “As we have consistently stated, FIFA has put in place rules which establish the framework for flights and travel by any FIFA official. The FIFA president routinely travels, together with relevant officials, on business and tournament-related matters and strives to visit member associations of FIFA whenever he can.

“Sometimes travel is organised on commercial (including low-cost) airlines and sometimes it is on private charter, depending on which is more efficient and cost-effective under the circumstances. FIFA pays travel costs.”

Sports.title: Leandro Paredes speaks out on Argentina World Cup conspiracy theories after sparking Spain brawl
Sports.content:
Leandro Paredes speaks out on Argentina World Cup conspiracy theories after sparking Spain brawl

Spain's World Cup win over Argentina in extra-time, thanks to a Ferran Torres goal, is the subject of conspiracy theories, with their opponents are now addressing them

View 2 Images Leandro Paredes has spoken out about the World Cup final back in Argentina (Image: Diego Alberto Haliasz, Getty Images)

Leandro Paredes believes Spain were worthy World Cup winners and is not entertaining talk of conspiracy theories after the final. Argentina's midfielder was central to the controversial scenes after Sunday's match, pushing and shoving multiple opposition players.

‌



Paredes, 32, is now back in his homeland, where he plays for Boca Juniors. Instead of taking a break like most of his international team-mates, he is already playing in South America, as the season has resumed after pausing for this summer's tournament.

‌



He played the full 90 minutes of their first game back. Paredes even assisted the game's only goal against O'Higgins.

‌



World Cup star allegedly tests positive for cocaine after double police stop READ MORE :

Jude Bellingham's parting shot to Argentina referee in unseen World Cup footage READ MORE :

Afterwards, he was inevitably asked about the World Cup. Conspiracy theories were among the topics of conversation.

Footage of Lionel Messi addressing his players before the match, urging them to "forget what happened", has sparked speculation that something suspicious took place. A clip of the incident doing the rounds on social media appears to show Enzo Fernandez and Lisandro Martinez visibly distressed as they emerge from the dressing room.

Martinez was substituted just before the break, apparently through injury, having already been booked. Fernandez departed early, too, after receiving his marching orders in the third minute of second-half stoppage time.

‌



View 2 Images Leandro Paredes lost his head after Argentina lost the World Cup final to Spain (Image: Al Bello, Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Paredes, however, has refused to entertain the rumours. In quotes reported by AS and translated into English from Spanish, he said: "Spain was superior to us in the final; they are a fair winner of the World Cup.

‌



"We don't give a damn about these theories. If it's what I hear, I have to go crazy.

"Everything that was said before, during and after the World Cup. We had a great tournament. We have to enjoy what we achieved in these eight years; it was a spectacular process. Surely we will fall when time passes because it is something incredible."

‌



He told ESPN: "For many, it will be a decision whether to continue or not. It was a spectacular process. It will be very difficult to maintain this level and keep the group functioning in this way. You have to think, take stock, and talk to the coach. Decisions must be made calmly. I don't know if I'm going to go on.

"I think it's going to be a long process to overcome what we experienced. Although we achieved a lot, the pain of losing the final is going to hurt for a long time, because we were very close again.

"But we have to enjoy it because it's not easy to maintain the level we had for so long to achieve what we did. Although we lost the final, I think we had a World Cup where the people saw themselves reflected, and for us that is very gratifying."

Sports.title: Devlin: Rangers wait was 'too stressful'
Sports.content:
Cammy Devlin revealed the stress he felt at the 2026 World Cup as he looked to make his move to Rangers.

After losing out on the Scottish Premiership title with Hearts on the last day of the season with a late defeat away to Celtic, who made it five in a row, the combative 28-year-old midfielder travelled to North America with Australia, who were knocked out of the tournament at the last-32 stage by Egypt on penalties.

Throughout his time with the Socceroos, speculation abounded about the possibility of teaming up again with manager Derek McInnes and captain Lawrence Shankland, who both made the move to Ibrox.

Image: Devlin has been reunited with his former captain Lawrence Shankland

On July 11, the day after Hearts confirmed Devlin would be leaving Tynecastle on freedom of contract, he signed for Rangers on a two-year deal with the option of a further year.

He made his first appearance in a blue jersey in the second half of Wednesday's 2-1 friendly win over St Etienne at Ibrox, where he impressed the Light Blues fans and manager McInnes.

Ahead of the Gers' final pre-season friendly against West Ham on Sunday, the Sydney-born player said: "Yeah, it was stressful to be honest.

"It was hard obviously. We didn't have much time to reflect on how last season ended and then it was straight into the World Cup, which is one of the most special moments of your career.

"My mum and dad and my girlfriend were over in America supporting me at the World Cup. You never think as a kid you would be lucky enough to be involved in that so you're trying to enjoy that as much as you can.

Image: Cammy Devlin was part of Australia's World Cup squad

"I thought it would be a good idea going in there off contract, but it wasn't. It was too stressful.

"It was hard to enjoy being in the moment and being at the World Cup and dealing with all that and all the noise around it. I had my dad asking me every day what's going on.

"But obviously everyone knows the relationship I have with the gaffer. We're super close.

"He was so good for me at Hearts. Everyone knows the season we had there last year and he helped me so much just as a player.

"So obviously I was speaking to him. And then when he got the job here, we had contact at the start, but not a whole lot.

Image: Devlin played under Rangers manager Derek McInnes at Hearts

"I can imagine when he became the Rangers manager, there was a lot more going on than just me and you've got to remember that.

"So I was trying not to focus too much on it and trying to, like I say, just enjoy the World Cup. But when the opportunity came, it was one that I thought was too good to pass up.

"Obviously being at Rangers is such a massive football club and that was kind of what happened for me. But like I say, it was pretty stressful. I'm glad now it's all over."

Rangers start life under McInnes at Dundee Utd

Rangers will begin life under Derek McInnes at Dundee United on July 31, live on Sky Sports.

The Friday night clash, which will kick-off at 8pm, marks the start of a groundbreaking opening weekend that will see all six Scottish Premiership games shown live on Sky Sports for the first time.

The fixture will be McInnes's first competitive match in charge after he replaced Danny Röhl as Rangers manager.

Sports.title: Leclerc fastest before stopping as Aston Martin hit early fault with new-look car
Sports.content:
Aston Martin's heavily upgraded car suffered a suspected suspension failure which spun Lance Stroll off track, as Ferrari Charles Leclerc set an impressive pace for Ferrari before running into his own technical trouble, during a highly eventful first practice session at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Leclerc outpaced Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton by half a second in a flying start to the Hungaroring weekend for the Monegasque driver with a best lap of 1:19.075.

But Leclerc's session ended seven minutes early when he had to stop at the top of the pit lane after reporting that "something broke" on his SF-26 car. Ferrari have not yet confirmed what went wrong.

Aston Martin, meanwhile, revealed 16 separate aerodynamic updates on their AMR26 car ahead of the session in the team's long-awaited first upgrade of a season which has hitherto seen them run at the back of the field.

But Stroll's session lasted just 11 laps after a suspected rear suspension failure pitched him off the road in a high-speed spin coming out of Turn Two.

The Canadian's car avoided contact with the barriers, but the team will now make the necessary repairs, and conduct investigations into what exactly went wrong, ahead of second practice at 4pm.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ted Kravitz looks at the upgrades Aston Martin have made ahead of the Hungarian Grand Prix

Team-mate Fernando Alonso, was, however, able to complete the session without apparent problem in the sister car, racking up 20 laps and finishing a promising 13th fastest.

That was 2.4 seconds behind Leclerc's pace but Aston Martin's deficit to the front has regularly been between three and four seconds in qualifying at recent events amid a lack of updates.

George Russell was fifth fastest, almost a second slower than Leclerc, in a session world championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli sat out so Mercedes could give another P1 outing to third driver Fred Vesti as part of the mandatory young driver requirements all teams must fulfil on four Fridays each season.

Vesti was seventh fastest, 0.4s away from Russell. Of the other rookies in action, reigning F2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli was 16th fastest in Oscar Piastri's McLaren, Ryo Hirakawa 17th in Oliver Bearman's Haas, Paul Aron 19th in Franco Colapinto's Alpine and Colton Herta 20th in Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac.

Isack Hadjar finished fourth quickest in the second Red Bull ahead of Russell and Audi's in-form Gabriel Bortoleto.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen fumes at Carlos Sainz after dangerously blocking his quick lap

Verstappen and Williams' Carlos Sainz must head to the stewards after the session, with both drivers charged with driving erratically following an incident early in the session.

Sainz initially got in Verstappen's way into Turn 12 before the Red Bull driver then seemed to slow in turn in front of the Williams once ahead through the corner.

Sainz will also be quizzed by the stewards about a second alleged incident of erratic driving later in the session involving Alpine rookie Aron at Turn Nine.

The Williams driver was slowest of all in an opening session which also included a huge lock-up into the first corner. A host of the drivers ran wide there to a greater or lesser extent during the hour, including Russell and Verstappen.

Sports.title: Scott: The 'scrawny-looking kid' turned complete midfielder wanted by the elite
Sports.content:
Across the seven games in which Bournemouth took points off Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea last season, it is telling that Alex Scott was nearly ever-present, playing 625 of a possible 630 minutes.

Scott was one of Andoni Iraola's most valued and trusted players in an historic season for the club. Clearly, he made a mark on their opponents too. Coveted by the elite, he could become the latest Premier League midfielder to make a high-profile move.

His future at Bournemouth is uncertain but it seems increasingly clear that the 22-year-old, nicknamed the 'Guernsey Grealish' as a teenager and described by Pep Guardiola as an "unbelievable player" as far back as 2023, has a bright future ahead of him.

'Scrawny-looking kid' turned duel-winner

Scott stands out for his technical ability. He boasts excellent close control and is comfortable in tight spaces. With his socks slung low around his ankles, and a capacity to glide away from defenders, the Jack Grealish comparisons are easy to understand.

Scott counts Grealish among his admirers. Like Guardiola, Grealish was left impressed by his performance in an FA Cup meeting between Manchester City and Bristol City when he was 19. "Top, top talent," wrote Grealish on social media after the game.

The technical qualities that stood out to Guardiola and Grealish that day had convinced Bristol City to pluck him from non-league Guernsey in the Channel Islands only a few years earlier in a move overseen by then director of youth recruitment Brian Tinnion.

Nigel Pearson, the manager who subsequently gave Scott his Championship debut, remembers him arriving as a "scrawny-looking youngster" with "incredible" talent. Before long, he was predicting Scott would one day represent England.

Scott is still waiting on his first cap. But he is a European Championship winner with England's U19s and U21s and a first senior call-up in November was followed by an invitation from Thomas Tuchel to join their pre-World Cup training camp in June.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alex Scott's best passes, tricks, tackles and goals for Bournemouth last season

Back at Bristol City, Scott handled the jump to the Championship impressively, making 35 starts in the competition in the 2021/22 campaign, then bettering his total with 40 in 2022/23. A £25m move to Bournemouth demanded another step up physically.

Scott was hindered by injuries in his first two seasons. He arrived at the Vitality Stadium in 2023 with a knee problem, then sustained another early in his second campaign at the club.

But his physical improvement has been evident across his time in the Premier League. Last season, he was finally deemed ready to become a regular starter and only missed one game for Bournemouth over the course of the campaign.

His ground duel success rate of 56 per cent was up from 47 per cent in his first season at Bournemouth and put him above Elliot Anderson, Bruno Guimaraes and Martin Zubimendi.

Scott's aerial success rate followed a similar trajectory, up from 44 per cent in his first campaign in the Premier League to 54 per cent last season. "He has really filled out and matured as a player," noted his former boss Pearson to Sky Sports.

Scott can now be viewed as one of the best ball-winners in the division in his position. Last season, only Anderson and Wolves' Andre won possession more times among midfielders. Scott also ranked in the top 10 for interceptions and duels won.

Ball-carrying and off-the-ball runs

Scott brought the same dynamism to Bournemouth's attack, with Iraola's team set up to allow as many opportunities as possible for him to utilise another of his strengths: his ball-carrying ability.

As well as being comfortable under pressure, Scott excels at attacking space, meaning the emphasis placed on maximising transitions and counters under Iraola suited his game perfectly.

Scott's total of 431 carries was the eighth-highest by a midfielder in the Premier League last season and around half of those carries were categorised by Opta as progressive, underlining his capacity to take his team up the pitch.

Scott's physical intensity shines through in his numbers relating to off-the-ball runs. According to Opta, Scott made the sixth-most supporting runs of all Premier League players last season.

One of the best examples came with his winning goal against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium in April, when Scott, having scanned his surroundings and identified an opportunity, charged through the middle of the pitch to be in a position to collect Evanilson's flick from David Brooks's pass before beating David Raya.

Iraola said Scott was becoming a "very complete" player after that game and there is evidence of that completeness in the tracking data. Scott's commitment to contributing at both ends of the pitch can be seen in the fact that he made more runs tracking back into position than any other Premier League player last term.

Scott also made the third-most high-speed runs in the division, and covered an incredible 27.6km at high speed, underlining the extent of his intensity as a box-to-box midfielder.

Best yet to come?

Iraola talked up Scott's ability to play in different positions last season. "He is playing as a six, as an eight, as a 10." And although the bulk of his minutes have come as an eight, his versatility is another strength. Scott was even used as a wing-back at Bristol City.

Image: Alex Scott has been used in a variety of different positions at Bournemouth

Scott's Premier League readiness is another factor which adds to his appeal. He has played 89 games in the competition over the last three seasons. But at only 22, there is also room for growth.

The main area for improvement is in front of goal.

Scott has only contributed four goals and three assists in those 89 Premier League appearances so far. Efforts to improve his output have been ongoing since his time in the second tier with Bristol City, when his numbers were similarly modest.

Image: Alex Scott celebrates his winning goal against Arsenal last season

"For him to be an eight or a 10, and for people to talk about him as an eight or a 10, he needed better numbers," Jason Euell, Pearson's assistant at Bristol City, told Sky Sports. "He wasn't getting enough assists and he wasn't scoring enough goals.

"He was doing it all in training, but never replicating it in games. When it was approaching one of the summer tournaments, I said, 'Look, it's great you've got so many Championship games under your belt, but if your numbers don't start changing, someone else is going to sneak up behind you and take your place.'"

Scott was able to fend off that competition. He played an important role in the U19 and U21 European Championship successes in 2022 and 2025. And while there remains a need for more goals and assists, Scott has proved he has plenty to offer.

Sports.title: Could Adeyemi's Barcelona move see Flick unlock winger's true potential?
Sports.content:
Perhaps Karim Adeyemi's move to Barcelona should not come as a surprise even if usurping Lamine Yamal as the team's star left-footed right-winger is impossible. After all, it was Hansi Flick, Barca’s head coach, who gave Adeyemi his debut for Germany.

The hope is that his old coach can spark something new in a player whose vast potential has been obvious for years but is yet to truly explode. This is an opportunity for Adeyemi to become the player that Flick and many others have long suspected he could be.

He was still a teenager with Red Bull Salzburg when Flick first picked him. But Adeyemi is only 24 now. If it feels like he has been around far longer it is because he had almost 100 games for Salzburg even before making the move to Borussia Dortmund in 2022.

Image: Karim Adeyemi during his official presentation as FC Barcelona's new player

He was playing for Salzburg's feeder team Liefering even before that, debuting at the age of 16. Speaking to Adeyemi about this during his time at Dortmund, he saw it as the ideal schooling. "For me, it was the best move that I could do," he told Sky Sports.

He explained: "The most important thing for a young guy is to play. They have a second team who play against adults. I played in the second league as a 16-year-old, a lot of games. I adapted to men's football and this is what is important for a young player."

Image: Karim Adeyemi had his moments during four years at Borussia Dortmund

There have been plenty of highlights since then. As one of those fortunate enough to be inside the Westfalenstadion when he raced clear to score a Champions League winner against Chelsea in 2023, it is fair to say that Adeyemi's pace leaves an impression.

He was clocked at a Bundesliga-high 36.65 kilometres per hour in that debut season. His reply when speaking to him about whether he was the fastest around was emphatic. "Yes, I am very confident with that." Is anyone close? "Close, maybe. But not faster."

The speed stats have tailed off slightly, although Adeyemi has still ranked among the fastest dozen Bundesliga players in each of the past two seasons. The bigger problem was that he was not quite able to evolve beyond that role of impact player at Dortmund.

Image: Karim Adeyemi's heat map and shot map in his Bundesliga career with Borussia Dortmund

There were moments. Adeyemi came on as a substitute to score a wonderful goal against Atalanta in the Champions League. He scored home and away against Stuttgart - both off the bench. The latter turned out to be his final goal in a Dortmund shirt.

But there has been criticism too. That was particularly the case in December when Adeyemi was substituted on the hour against Borussia Monchengladbach and reacted badly. Former Germany international Markus Babbel publicly questioned his mentality.

Within Dortmund, there are those who defend him. He is a popular figure with staff past and present. Speaking to Alex Clapham, their former set-piece coach, he saw Adeyemi as a particular favourite. "He is an incredible guy. What a character," he told Sky Sports.

"As a coach, he probably taught me more than anybody because I had to work with him in a different way. It probably took me until Christmas of the first season to understand that." Adeyemi responded better to one-on-ones. "It is the little chats sometimes."

Image: It was Hansi Flick who gave Karim Adeyemi his Germany debut in 2021

Flick will understand that better than anyone. And this is why the move to Barcelona could unlock more from the player. This is a coach who has believed in his talent from a young age and always championed him. It is great for Adeyemi. But what about Barca?

It might seem incongruous given the scale of the club, but the expectation levels might be a little lower. At Dortmund, there was some frustration that Adeyemi did not grow into the role of the team's star player. That is clearly not the assignment at Camp Nou.

Barcelona do not need someone to lead the attack. This is a team that scored 95 goals in LaLiga last season, 18 more than Real Madrid. What they need is someone who can impact off the bench, cover across a range of different positions, make a contribution.

Image: Karim Adeyemi's minutes by position for Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga

"I can play in almost any position in the offensive line," Adeyemi told Sky Sports back in that 2023 interview. Since then, he has operated on both flanks and occasionally in the centre. Marcus Rashford did a similar job last season. There will certainly be minutes for him.

In fact, his role could be really important for Barcelona. Consider the template set by Paris Saint-Germain. The former Barca player Ousmane Dembele started only 11 games in Ligue 1 last season. He actually started as many games in the Champions League.

Perhaps it is easier to load the emphasis on European commitments in France than Spain but compare that to Lamine Yamal, who played 26 games from the start in La Liga last season. That was more than any midfielder or attacker in the Barcelona squad.

The chance to rest the star man, after a World Cup in which he went all the way with Spain while Adeyemi was omitted from Germany's campaign, is one that Flick will need to take when and where he can. He will want to be able to do so with minimal disruption.

Flick loves having pace in wide areas. Barcelona still play a possession game under him. Indeed, they averaged 69 per cent possession in La Liga last season, the highest in Europe's five major leagues - even ahead of Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

But Flick needs his team to have that speed to go with it. It is this that helps Barcelona break teams down, providing the counter-attacking threat as well as the domination of the ball. Adeyemi suits that style of play. He is someone who can make things happen.

Asking him how he saw his game, he said: "I think [my job is] to get on the nerves of the defenders all the time with one-against-one or runs behind the defenders. Being there where the defender cannot see me. Getting assists, getting goals. This, I think, is my game."

Adeyemi is at a crossroads in his career now. Raphinha was already 25 when he moved to Barcelona from Leeds and changed perspectives about his potential ceiling. Adeyemi is younger. With the right coach, at the right club, the sky is still the limit for him.

Sports.title: Maresca says managing Manchester City ‘a privilege’ but admits challenge of following Guardiola
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca said following Pep Guardiola as Manchester City manager is a “privilege” but admitted he is aware how the successors to Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsène Wenger struggled at Manchester United and Arsenal.

Maresca took over at City last month and, at his first press conference in the role, said he understands the challenge of replacing Guardiola, who claimed 17 major trophies in his decade in charge to become the club’s greatest ever manager.

The Italian said: “First of all, I have to say that it’s a privilege because the club decided to go for me. I said many times that I consider Pep probably the best coach in the world in the last 20, 25 years.”

Maresca pointed to how United dipped when David Moyes replaced Ferguson, who was in charge for 26 and a half years, in May 2013. Arsenal also struggled when Wenger departed after 22 years in May 2018, being replaced by Unai Emery.

Maresca said: “It’s a challenge. It’s nice. Also, the history of the manager with many years in the same club always struggled a little bit. After Sir Alex, after Arsène. But also, it’s a challenge to try to do the right things immediately for this organisation, for the fans, for everyone.”

Maresca believes City’s structure gives him the best chance of success. “The organisation is the main thing. This club, this organisation, they had three managers in 17 years,” he said of Guardiola, Manuel Pellegrini and Roberto Mancini. “This is not normal. It doesn’t happen often.

“I’m confident that we can do a great job. We can continue to do the job that has been done since Roberto was here, then after Manuel and for 10 years Pep.”

Maresca confirmed that Rodri will have back surgery on Monday, so is set to miss the start of the season. The new City manager was asked whether the 30-year-old’s future remains at the club, with Real Madrid considering a move for the player.

“First of all, around big players there is always speculation,” Maresca said. “I’m not worried about that. Also because they [Spain] won the World Cup and he was the best player or one of the best players, I think every manager wants to have Rodri because he’s a top player.

“But now he has surgery on, I think, Monday. He needs holiday, rest. Then he will be back here with us.”

The manager added that James Trafford, the second-choice goalkeeper who is of interest to Leeds, and Jack Grealish, who has returned to City after last season’s loan at Everton, could both depart.

Maresca said: “Jack, at the moment, he’s a Man City player. I always said the same – in any club I join, I like to know if there are players that belong to the club, it’s my duty to try to coach them. Then we see what happens.

“I know James because he was my keeper when I was with the City Under-23s [in 2020-21]. But again, when the transfer window is open now, January, anything can happen. So we see. But at the moment, he’s one of our keepers.”

Sports.title: Jürgen Klopp vows to change Germany but threatens to quit if family hounded by media
Sports.content:
Jürgen Klopp said he wants his team to “change a country” after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach, but threatened to stand down if his family are hounded by the media during his time in charge.

In a forthright first press conference upon his unveiling as Julian Nagelsmann’s replacement, Klopp also suggested the role will be his final job in top-level football and expressed regret after poking fun at his predecessor while working as a television pundit during the World Cup. He is tasked with reviving Germany, who lost to Paraguay in the last 32 and have not made the last 16 since winning the tournament in 2014.

It marks a return to the dugout for Klopp two years after leaving Liverpool, where he ended a glorious nine-season tenure after explaining he felt fatigued. Since January 2025 he has worked as head of global soccer for Red Bull but a comeback to frontline action had appeared inevitable since Nagelsmann departed on 3 July.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp was in forthright mood in his first press conference as Germany head coach. Photograph: Hannes Albert/EPA

Klopp vowed to transform a deeply fractured relationship between the national team and Germany’s public, citing his work at Liverpool as an example of the way football can galvanise a wider community.

“I want to create a situation where fans go home after the game and say: ‘Wow, that was cool,’” he said. “I want people to say: ‘Wow, it was worth putting the TV on for 90 minutes to see Germany play.’ I’ve lived and experienced how football can change a city. And I think it’s not only about cities, it’s also about the country. Ideally, football can change a country.”

The 59-year-old’s contract will run until after the 2030 World Cup. Klopp, however, warned that he would not tolerate invasive treatment from journalists and that he would be prepared to depart without compensation if he felt his family’s privacy had been violated.

“I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you treated Nagelsmann,” he said. “I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you’ve treated, in England, Thomas Tuchel. The day you don’t want me any more, I’m gone, without any severance pay. If you say tomorrow: ‘He’s shit,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away.

“Criticise me if something doesn’t work. Jürgen Klopp is not going to have any career after the national team. This is the pinnacle of my career as a coach. I will give it everything I’ve got.”

Klopp was criticised last month when, speaking with the former Germany player Thomas Müller on television during coverage of the group stage match with Curaçao, he appeared to hint Nagelsmann’s days were numbered by saying he was “still” picking the team. That was followed by a quick apology; Klopp repeated the sentiment on Friday and said the pair have yet to speak since his appointment was confirmed.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp, in his role as Magenta TV pundit, with Kylian Mbappé after France’s World Cup quarter-final against Morocco. Photograph: Greg M Cooper/EPA

“We haven’t had any exchange,” he said, wishing Nagelsmann a happy 39th birthday for Thursday. “It was a joke. In retrospect it was one of the worst ‘funny’ remarks I have ever made. I feel awfully sorry, I’ve apologised a million times.

“It was just a rash thing to say, with no ulterior motive whatsoever, and I can only wish him the best.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Now he can go on to pastures new and I’m absolutely sure he will have many opportunities to coach a big team in future.”

Klopp promised Germany will play expansive football with wingers but admitted they must find their own way to compete with the depth of talent available elsewhere. “Success is performance relative to expectations,” he said. “When we ask in Germany: ‘Are we as good as France?’ and the answer is no, that’s not true. If we ask: ‘Do we have players like Dembélé, Mbappé, Doué and Barcola?’, no we don’t, but we can still beat them.

“We don’t want to play like Argentina, Spain, England or France. We want to do it the German way, very intense. Are we the No 1 team right now? No, we accept that. There are 11 teams ahead of us in the ranking. We can beat them, but for this to happen we need to play very good, very intense football.”

International football will demand a change of rhythm for Klopp after a lifetime spent in the domestic game. “I think contact with a team is not necessarily about working with them day in, day out,” he said. “Sometimes it will be 30 minutes or an hour and that will be on the pitch. But all of them have a mobile. I’ll talk to them, listen to them, watch games and give my feedback. That, too, is developing players and making them better.”

Klopp’s reign will begin with a ­baptism of fire in Amsterdam against the Netherlands on 24 September, one of four Nations League games in the space of 11 days. “The players have to show me, and not just say it, that playing for Germany is a super special thing,” he said.

Sports.title: Manchester United and the quest to make mythical midfield a reality
Sports.content:
MIDDLE MEN

Like the urban myth that you are never more than three feet away from a spider, modern footballing lore tells us Manchester United are only ever three signings away from a Premier League title challenge. With the Geopolitics World Cup in the rear-view mirror and the transfer news machine churning once more, you may have missed United being linked with just about every midfielder to ever grace a centre circle. They missed out on Elliot Anderson – who went and dubbed his new club the “kings of Manchester” – and were fooled into thinking they could snare Aurélien Tchouaméni. They danced briefly with Atalanta’s Éderson, before landing on Chelsea resale project prospect Andrey Santos and former Aston Villa linchpin Youri Tielemans. And United aren’t done with their midfield overhaul – rightly so given they have lost Casemiro to Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte to long-term knee knack. Next up on United’s extensive longlist: Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga and Fulham’s Sander Berge, plus France GWC sensation Manu Koné as Michael Carrick eyes the final piece in his midfield puzzle.

The problem with United over the past 13 years has been that it’s never actually the final piece. It would be kind to call their post-Ferguson transfer hit rate scattergun. Ángel Di María was the first final piece in the puzzle. Then it was Alexis Sánchez. Then Fred. And then Jadon Sancho. Something needed to change. So say what you like about Big Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s recent, purse-tightening Old Trafford regime, but they’ve not flopped anywhere near as hard in the transfer market as their predecessors. Only Ugarte and Joshua Zirkzee can be deemed true flops under the Ineos boys. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha were smart additions a year ago, Senne Lammens was a scouting triumph and United are threatening to go again with their sensible signings policy – who’d have thunk it?! – with a combined £85m on Santos and Tielemans representing far better value than splashing that same amount on relegation specialist Matheus Fernandes. Finding value in the market is almost impossible nowadays, but credit to these fellas, they’re giving it a go.

What feels quite apt with Carrick at the wheel is that United’s biggest struggle this summer has been to find a true midfield destroyer. That moniker certainly doesn’t fit Santos, nor Tielemans. Tchouaméni was always unattainable so United are getting creative, as they did when Carrick was sought as Roy Keane’s replacement in 2006, less a like-for-like replacement and more a style shift. OK, it could be argued that Berge – an experienced screening No 6 – could step into the Casemiro void after a promising GWC campaign, but Camavinga and Koné like to charge around putting out fires, so perhaps United are following the mould of other top clubs and dispensing with the idea of the Makélélé role.

Modern football is all about excess, whether that be GWC participants, number of games, or transfer fees going beyond £100m for apparently workmanlike players. United have long threatened to descend into financial overspill, but after a steady season under a steady manager, are they finally grasping the concept of modest frugality? Roll up, roll up: ditch the merch-baiting marquee signing and grab yourself three all-purpose midfielders, all for reasonable prices! It surely cannot last.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“This is ideally the high point of my career, of my life, my professional life. I will give it everything I have [but] if you [reporters] tomorrow start saying: ‘He’s sh!t,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away” – Jürgen Klopp takes the Germany job and proves that he should still be good for a quote or two.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp: still got it. Photograph: Markus Ulmer/GES Sportfoto/Getty Images

Paolo Maldini, the Italian football federation’s new technical director, revealed talks with Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti have been held as the crisis-hit nation seek a new managerial figurehead. “We can’t hide that we also talked with Carlo Ancelotti before talking with Pep,” he tooted. Reports have since suggested Guardiola may have turned the Azzurri down.

Spain’s head coach, Luis De la Fuente, has slammed the behaviour of Argentina’s players after the conclusion of the GWC final. “It is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed,” he boomed.

According to Home Office figures, there was a 4% increase in the number of matches with reports of “football-related anti-social behaviour, violence and disorder” during the 2025-26 season.

Senegal’s appeal against the removal of their Africa Cup of Nations title will be heard by Cas on 8 October – almost eight months after the final.

The transfer wheels keep on turning. Alejandro Garnacho has found a (temporary) new home on loan at Aston Villa, while Chelsea have agreed a deal to sign Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix, and Newcastle have signed Monaco midfielder Aladji Bamba for a fee that could rise to £34m.

And Jermain Defoe’s Woking are no longer Jermain Defoe’s Woking. The former Spurs and England striker has left the National League side after an “eye-opening” 116 days at the helm. “Unfortunately, circumstances have ultimately made it impossible for me to continue in the position,” Defoe sighed in a Social Media Disgrace post.

YOU SAY TOMATO

Some GWC underachievers might be alarmed to see crates of tomatoes waiting for them after their flight home – but there were no such worries for Fabián Ruiz and Gavi as they returned to their home town. The Spain midfielders both hail from Los Palacios y Villafranca, a town of 40,000 people that has now produced three World Cup winners, Ruiz and Gavi joining Jesús Navas in the hall of fame. There are plans for a permanent monument to all three men in the Andalucían town, but for now, they’ll have to make do with *checks notes* their own body weight in tomatoes – 85kg for Ruiz, 68.5kg for Gavi. Local officials say the tradition “is a hallmark of the municipality for honouring its great athletes.” And don’t they look delighted.

Sports.title: Newcastle sign Aladji Bamba in £34m deal from Monaco to boost midfield options
Sports.content:
Newcastle have made Aladji Bamba their fourth signing of the summer after the 20-year-old midfielder completed a move from Monaco for a fee that could rise to £34m.

“I’m very happy to be here,” said Bamba. “I was very excited when I heard Newcastle were interested in signing me. I know about the history of the club and I’ve visited the stadium, which is amazing. I can’t wait to be on the pitch.”

Bamba, who has agreed a five-year contract, is Newcastle’s fourth signing this summer aged 20 or under. The France youth midfielder – who made 25 appearances for Monaco last season, impressing in Ligue 1 and the Champions League – joins the former Reims goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (20), the former Hoffenheim winger Bazoumana Touré (also 20) and the former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur (18). As a natural No 6, Bamba will be expected to compete with Lewis Miley for the midfield anchor role vacated when Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham for an initial £92.5m.

Newcastle’s transfer policy is to sign players aged 24 or under costing, broadly, between £20m and £40m and possessing high resale potential. The idea is to help ensure a club that has recently negotiated a three-year settlement agreement with Uefa after breaching European spending rules remain on the right side of football’s squad investment regulations. “Aladji adds a range of qualities to our midfield with huge potential for growth,” said Eddie Howe, Newcastle’s manager. “His development since breaking through at Monaco has been really impressive and is something we believe we can build on.”

Meanwhile, Howe hopes Bruno Guimarães will be at Newcastle to ease Bamba’s adaptation to Premier League life. The Brazil midfielder is wanted by Arsenal and appears keen to join Mikel Arteta’s team. However, the price is a stumbling block. Newcastle’s reluctance to sell their captain dictates they have let it be known through intermediaries that they will reject any offer in the region of £70m for a player who turns 29 in November.

Arsenal have still to make a formal offer and whether they are prepared to go beyond £75m remains to be seen. Much may hinge on whether Guimarães returns to Newcastle from a holiday in Brazil, as planned, next week before joining his teammates at a training camp at La Manga in southern Spain.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola backs backroom staff to help cure Liverpool’s set-piece ills
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season and admitted he was “very lucky” to inherit a talented coaching team at Bournemouth.

Iraola has brought several members of his Bournemouth backroom team with him to Liverpool since succeeding Arne Slot last month. Tommy Elphick, a boyhood Liverpool fan, and Shaun Cooper have joined as first-team coaches while Iraola’s long-time colleague Pablo de la Torre has arrived as assistant coach. Alejandro Rosalen has taken over as first-team goalkeeping coach after five years with Napoli.

Iraola worked alongside De la Torre in his first coaching job at AEK Larnaca, and again at Rayo Vallecano, and said having trusted confidants alongside him would be invaluable for his first season in charge at Anfield. “For me, it was important they came with me,” said Iraola, who will take charge of his first Liverpool game on Saturday in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville. “Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching. So, for me, he is much more than a physical coach really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.

“I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth. Because I was unlucky to have the issue with my assistant coach Iñigo Pérez [who was denied a work permit when attempting to follow Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth]. After, it worked out very well for him because now he is coaching Villarreal. Maybe we play him in the Champions League.

“But when I had Tommy and Shaun there, we did not feel the need to bring in another assistant. They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different. Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield; they can be in a closer position to the players. They can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn’t know I was a player.”

One requirement for Iraola and his backroom staff will be to address Liverpool’s problems at set pieces. Only Bournemouth (26), Crystal Palace (25) and Leeds (24) conceded more set-piece goals than Liverpool’s 23 in what proved Slot’s final season as head coach, having won the title in his first. “They are very good coaches,” said Iraola. “We kind of ­understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.

“Tommy does defensive set plays, Shaun does more offensive, more ­creative ones. But also we are working very well here with the set-piece analyst [Lewis Mahoney], who was very good in the second half of last season. He is already with the club, so they are working on some stuff.”

Sports.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
Sports.content:
Spain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final.

At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, who attacked Rodri and Eric García respectively at New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebrated winning the World Cup for a second time in the country’s history. Paredes also confronted Spain’s Gavi.

“At the time, I didn’t realise it. I was celebrating, hugging teammates,” De La Fuente told Spanish television. “But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed. Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.”

De la Fuente also praised the exemplary behaviour of his own players faced with these “acts of aggression” and “provocations” which he believes could have escalated into more serious incidents.

Although the scenes were filmed and widely shared on social media, they have not yet resulted in any sanctions against the Argentina players. Fifa has opened an investigation into the incidents to determine whether there may have been violations of the world football governing body’s disciplinary code.

Sports.title: From Popp to Diani: 10 women’s transfers you may have missed during the men’s World Cup
Sports.content:
There were a host of big women’s football transfers which were hard to miss across June and July, despite the dominance of the men’s World Cup. Among them were Beth Mead’s move from Arsenal to Manchester City, Mary Earps and Georgia Stanway returning to the Women’s Super League with London City Lionesses and Arsenal, Sam Kerr leaving Chelsea to return to Gotham FC and, most prominently, Alexia Putellas’s game-changing switch from Barcelona to London City.

But here are 10 transfers you might have missed while attention was focused on the action in the US, Canada and Mexico.

Alexandra Popp to Borussia Dortmund

The three-time Champions League winner Alex Popp may be reaching the twilight of her playing career but her move to Borussia Dortmund, signing a three-year contract at the tier-three club, after 14 years with Wolfsburg shows she is not quite ready to hang up her boots. The 35-year-old has been prolific for club and country, scoring 112 goals in 219 games for Wolfsburg and 67 goals in 145 games for Germany prior to her international retirement in 2024. A Borussia Dortmund fan whose “heart beats for this club”, Popp couldn’t pass up the opportunity to assist the development of the women’s team, which was launched in 2020.

Kirsty Hanson to Tottenham

The 28-year-old was a top target for Spurs after a phenomenal fourth season at Aston Villa. Last year Hanson said she was working on adding more goals to her game – come the end of last season she was the third-highest top scorer in the WSL, finishing on 12 in 22 games, which was 43% of Villa’s total tally and only one goal behind second-place Alessia Russo. She heads to a focused Tottenham who are giving their manager, Martin Ho, the tools to push closer to, or even break into, the top four.

Ally Sentnor to Angel City

Sentnor, who was the first overall pick in the 2024 NWSL draft, was the subject of a blockbuster $850,000 (£635,000) trade between Kansas City Current and Angel City on 19 June. She then made her debut for her new side on 3 July, starting a 2-0 win against Orlando Pride. The USA women’s national team player has scored seven goals and provided three assists in 23 international games and, at just 22 years old, has a lot of football ahead of her.

View image in fullscreen Ally Sentnor (right) on the ball for Angel City in a 2-0 win against against Chicago Stars last weekend. Photograph: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/Shutterstock

Felicia Schröder to Real Madrid

Many clubs were circling but in the end Felicia Schröder completed a big-money move from Häcken to Real Madrid. Multiple Swedish outlets reported the deal for the 19-year-old forward was worth over 15m Swedish kronor (£1.15m). She attracted attention from across the world as she racked up 91 goals in 128 games for Häcken and starred in Uefa’s inaugural women’s Europa Cup competition, finishing as top scorer with eight goals, four of which came in the two-legged final against Hammarby.

Manaka Matsukubo to Chelsea

The versatile 21-year-old, who can play as a forward or attacking midfielder, joined Chelsea from North Carolina Courage for an undisclosed fee but, as one of the most exciting young talents in the women’s game, it’s unlikely she came cheap. The Japan international scored 11 goals, became the youngest NWSL player to score a hat-trick, and was named NWSL midfielder of the year in 2025. She was up to five goals in nine games in the 2026 season before Chelsea swooped earlier this month.

View image in fullscreen Manaka Matsukubo at her Chelsea unveiling. Photograph: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Johanna Rytting Kaneryd to OL Lyonnes

The 29-year-old won three league titles, two FA Cups and two League Cups with Chelsea, including a domestic treble in . Rytting Kaneryd is one of several attacking players to leave Chelsea this summer with Sam Kerr, Guro Reiten and Catarina Macario also having departed as they revamp their front line in an effort to reclaim their WSL crown after Manchester City ended their six-year title-winning run.

Noémie Mouchon to Everton

The loss of the forward Kelly Gago, who has signed for West Ham, has been tempered a little by the arrival of the French striker Noémie Mouchon from Leicester. Mouchon did not have the easiest time at Leicester after arriving from Reims with expectations high. The 23-year-old sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury one month into her first season in the WSL and was ruled out for the remainder of the campaign. She made 16 appearances and scored two goals in the WSL last season but made only two starts. Everton will be hoping she can find the form that helped her to nine goals in 22 games for Reims in the 2023-24 season.

Denise O’Sullivan to Gotham (on loan)

The influential Republic of Ireland midfielder returns to the NWSL with Gotham after six months with Liverpool. The 32-year-old spent 10 seasons in the US before her January move to Liverpool, with Houston Dash and North Carolina Courage (albeit with a number of loan spells in Australia and England). She won the NWSL Shield in 2017 and again in 2018 and 2019 when Courage also secured the NWSL Championship, with O’Sullivan named the side’s MVP in both years. She has 22 goals in 132 games for Ireland.

View image in fullscreen Denise O’Sullivan (right) showing off her close control against Aston Villa last season. Photograph: Nick Taylor/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Bethany England to Crystal Palace

Bethany England’s Tottenham departure was mourned by fans, with the former Chelsea forward having become the team’s record goalscorer in the WSL with 32 in three-and-a-half seasons, helping them to a first FA Cup final in 2024. The 32-year-old has signed a two-year contract with Crystal Palace, who earned promotion back into the top flight with a second-place finish in WSL2. After four WSL titles, two FA Cups and two League Cups with Chelsea, England brings a wealth of experience to Palace.

Kadidiatou Diani to London City Lionesses

The arrival of Alexia Putellas and Mary Earps has dominated the London City Lionesses transfer talk, while the acquisition of the France forward Kadidiatou Diani from Lyonnes for more than £500,000 has flown somewhat under the radar. The 31-year-old scored 41 goals in 93 games in three seasons for the Champions League giants following her stunning 92 goals in 168 games for Paris Saint-Germain. Michelle Kang, who owns both London City and Lyonnes, will be hoping she brings that edge up front to the ambitious WSL side. They finished sixth last season, their debut campaign in the top flight, nine points behind Tottenham, but they want more and are spending big to make progress.

Sports.title: Socceroos star Cristian Volpato allegedly tests positive for cocaine during roadside test
Sports.content:
Socceroos forward Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped while driving at almost 50km/h over the speed limit in Sydney.

Volpato was one of Australia’s breakout stars of the 2026 World Cup but is now back in the spotlight after allegedly driving a BMW Coupe at 109km/h in a 60km/h zone across Anzac Bridge about 1.10am on Friday.

The 22-year-old was subjected to a roadside drug test which allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine. A secondary sample of oral fluid was taken for further analysis, while NSW police confirmed it will continue its inquiries.

Volpato was reportedly issued an infringement notice for speeding and has had his international driver’s licence suspended for six months, meaning he cannot drive in New South Wales. He has not been charged with a criminal offence.

Police allege that Volpato was also stopped two hours earlier on Anzac Bridge, west of Sydney’s CBD, and issued an infringement notice after allegedly driving more than 20km/h over the speed limit.

He was subjected to a roadside alcohol breath test at about 11.05pm Thursday, which returned a negative result.

Football Australia has been contacted for comment.

Volpato plays football for Italian club Sassuolo and represented Italy at at under-19 and under-20 level before switching his international allegiance to Australia on the eve of the World Cup.

He made three appearances for the Socceroos at the tournament and provided an attacking threat as the side progressed from the group stage as runners-up before being knocked out by Egypt in the last 32.

Volpato was born and raised in Sydney and played junior football at Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney Wanderers before moving overseas to join Serie A club Roma.

He left Roma after two seasons to join Sassuolo where he has scored seven goals in three seasons, before making his mark with the Socceroos and shaping up as a key to the national side’s future.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca vows not to let Man City crumble like at Man United when Sir Alex Ferguson left as he delights at sealing Man City return to replace Pep Guardiola following Chelsea exit
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca vows not to let Man City crumble like at Man United when Sir Alex Ferguson left as he delights at sealing Man City return to replace Pep Guardiola following Chelsea exit

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Enzo Maresca says it’s a privilege to succeed Pep Guardiola as Manchester City manager and is confident the empire he built won’t collapse like it did at Manchester United when Sir Alex Ferguson retired.

Guardiola won 20 trophies during his decade in charge at the Etihad before deciding to walk away at the end of last season. Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant and City’s elite development system coach during his two previous stints at the club, is relishing the chance to succeed him.

The 46-year-old Italian believes he can maintain City’s success because the club has been so well run under Guardiola, Manuel Pellegrini and Roberto Mancini, and there is no danger of a slump as United and Arsenal suffered when Ferguson and Arsene Wenger left.

‘I have to say that it's a privilege, because the reason why the club decided to go for me means that for me it's a privilege,’ said Maresca at his official unveiling on Friday.

‘I consider Pep probably the best coach in the world in the last 20-25 years. But again, it's a challenge. It's nice. It's a privilege. Also, the history of the manager with many years in the same club, always struggling a bit afterwards, after Sir Alex and after Arsene. It's a challenge to try to do the right things immediately for this organisation, for the fans, for everyone.

‘I think the organisation is the main thing. This club, this organisation, they had three managers in 17 years. This is not normal. It does not happen often. So this probably is one of the things that I'm confident why we can do a great job. We can continue to do the job that has been done in the last probably 14, 15 years since Roberto was here, Mancini, then after Manuel for 10 years Pep.’

Enzo Maresca was unveiled to the media as Manchester City boss on Friday

Maresca succeeded Pep Guardiola as City boss, signing a three year deal at the Etihad

Maresca was reluctant to be drawn on his departure from Chelsea in January which ended with City paying their Premier League rivals £17million in compensation after they appointed him as Guardiola’s successor.

‘I have been quite lucky in terms of my former clubs, Leicester and Chelsea,’ added Maresca, who won the Club World Cup and UEFA Conference League at Stamford Bridge. ‘I think we did a great job in both clubs. The identity of the team was clear. The success of the team was clear, and I feel very lucky to be part of these clubs. But now I think we are here today. That is the most important thing. Just about City. Nothing to add.’

The new manager was asked about City midfielder Rodri who continues to be linked with a move to Real Madrid after entering the final year of his contract at the Etihad. The Spaniard is due to undergo surgery on a back injury after winning the World Cup earlier this month.

‘First of all, we have to say that around big players, there are always speculations,’ said Maresca. ‘I'm not worried about that, I think it's normal. Also, because they won the World Cup, he was the best player or one of the best players.

‘I think every manager wants to have Rodri because he's a top player. But (he will have) surgery on Monday, and he needs a holiday. He needs to rest. He needs to recover, and then he will be back here with us.’

"I think every manager wants to have Rodri"



Enzo Maresca gives an update on Rodri following Spain's win in the World Cup 💬 pic.twitter.com/xsotBmJ2Ro — Sky Sports News (@SkySportsNews) July 24, 2026

Maresca is a disciple of Pep Guardiola, having worked as his assistant for their treble-winning season in 2022-23

He was also asked about the futures of goalkeeper James Trafford, who has been linked with Leeds, and Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Everton.

‘I know James because he was my keeper when I was with the Under-23s,’ replied Maresca. ‘So I know James very well. But again, it's when the transfer window is open, now and in January, anything can happen. So we’ll see. But at the moment, he’s one of our keepers.

‘Jack, at the moment, this year, he's Man City player. I always said the same. In any club I join, if there are players that belong to the club it's my duty to try to coach them.

‘I have a good relation with Jack. Since I left we kept in touch, and the reason why is because he has a big heart and is a very good guy. So this is the reason why. And then we see what happens.’

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp confirmed as Germany manager - and has already threatened to QUIT after World Cup's 'most controversial WAG' was criticised: 'If you don't leave my family in peace, I'm gone'
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jurgen Klopp has been unveiled as Germany manager – and has already revealed what will make him quit the job.

The Liverpool legend, 59, is back in the dugout having enjoyed a stint overseeing Red Bull's football operation after leaving Anfield in 2024, and has been tasked with turning the national team around after another disappointing major tournament.

Julian Nagelsmann was given his marching orders after the Germans crashed out to Paraguay in the Round of 32, leading to an inquest into the team's performance –where the players' WAGs and families were placed under the spotlight.

Nagelsmann's partner also made headlines, with German media reporting that his girlfriend, Lena Wurzenberger, was an almost constant presence in the camp.

But Klopp has already set his stall in a robust unveiling, insisting that he will quit the job immediately if his family face any scrutiny.

'The day you don't want me anymore, you say so and I'm gone, without severance pay,' he said via Bild.

'If you say tomorrow that he's rubbish, I'm gone. Not just one person, it would have to be more than that. If the DFB says he's rubbish, I'm gone. If you behave badly and don't leave my family in peace, I'm gone.'

Jurgen Klopp is Germany's new manager, but has already set out what will make him quit

Klopp says he will leave if the media 'don't leave my family in peace' after his predecessor Julian Nagelsmann's relationship with an ex-reporter made headlines

Klopp also described his appointment to the national team position as 'the highlight of my career'.

'Criticise me if something doesn't work. I'm happy to work on it. It's all about the job. Jurgen Klopp doesn't have a career after the national team. Ideally, this is the highlight of my career.'

Wurzenberger, 34, reportedly caused 'quite a stir' among the squad after being 'more present than probably any national team's coach before her'.

She was first spotted at Germany's pre-tournament camp in Frankfurt, when she was pictured watching training from a balcony along with a host of the players' partners.

And after her boyfriend's side thumped Curacao 7-1 - Wurzenberger hung around to watch the German substitutes complete their warm down.

It was then reported that she accompanied Nagelsmann back to the team hotel, before the duo were seen cycling to training together the following morning.

'There is naturally always that feeling that when the boss's wife is in the room, you might not always be completely honest at the table when talking about the national coach,' local reporters speculated during the tournament.

Klopp met second wife Ulla Sandrock in 2005 and married her that same year

Wurzenberger, and indeed Nagelsmann, also incited criticism from Germany legend Lothar Matthaus, who admitted her constant presence is far from 'ideal'.

The midfielder, who earned 150 caps, said on German television: 'She just shouldn't appear in the pictures too often - that wouldn't be ideal in my opinion.

'The players have days off and their families can come to the hotel. Lena (Wurzenberger) did that too. From my perspective, I think it's perfectly normal.

'Lena was able to come to the hotel just like the players' girlfriends and wives. You can see the solidarity - but the rule shouldn't apply to the coach. It has to happen during the time when we players are seeing their families.'

Nagelsmann and Wurzenberger are reported to have started dating soon after he split from his ex-wife Verena, following 15 years together, in 2022.

At that point Nagelsmann was manager of German giants Bayern Munich - and his new love interest reported on the club for Bild.

An article from the publication announcing their romance read: 'Julian Nagelsmann loves Bild reporter'.

Klopp married social worker and children's writer Ulla Sandrock in December 2005, having met at a pub during an Oktoberfest celebration that same year. He was previously married to ex-wife Sabine, with whom he shares a child.

Elsewhere, Arsenal legend Per Mertesacker will play an integral role in Klopp's transformation of the German national team, having been appointed the new Managing Director of Sport for the federation.

Sports.title: Australian World Cup star allegedly tests positive for cocaine just weeks after earning national hero status at the tournament
Sports.content:
Australian World Cup star allegedly tests positive for cocaine just weeks after earning national hero status at the tournament

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Australian footballer Cristian Volpato has allegedly returned a positive roadside drug test for cocaine, just weeks after representing his country at the World Cup.

The 22-year-old became one of Australia’s most popular athletes during the Socceroos’ World Cup run to the Round of 32, where they were eliminated by Egypt.

He is now also alleged to have been caught speeding twice on Sydney’s Anzac Bridge in the space of two hours.

At about 11.05pm on Thursday July 23, police officers stopped Volpato, driving his BMW Coupe, allegedly travelling at least 25km/h over the 60km/h speed limit.

He returned a negative breath test, before being issued an infringement notice for allegedly exceeding the speed limit by more than 20km/h.

Just over two hours later, police allegedly stopped Volpato again.

Cristian Volpato (pictured) is alleged to have returned a positive roadside drug test for cocaine

The 22-year-old (pictured) has subsequently seen his license suspended for six months

Volpato (pictured) was one of the Socceroos' breakout stars in the recent World Cup event

They did so after he was allegedly travelling at 109km/h in the same 60km/h zone.

Officers then subjected the Socceroos star to a roadside drug test, which police allege returned a positive result for cocaine.

Volpato has since been issued another infringement notice for allegedly exceeding the speed limit by more than 45km/h.

His international driver’s licence has also been suspended for six months.

‘Traffic and Highway Patrol Command officers will continue to target dangerous driving behaviour, including excessive speeding, to keep NSW roads safe,’ NSW Police told The Daily Mail in a statement.

‘Drivers are reminded that speeding and driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol can have devastating consequences for themselves and other road users.’

Football Australia has been contacted for comment.

A promising youngster, Volpato was the subject of an international tug-of-war between Australia and Italy when he rose through the ranks at Roma.

Volpato, who was born and raised in Sydney and played his youth football Down Under, represented Italy at U19 and U20 level before committing to Australia's senior team.

He said he was happy to 'wait for Italy' after he was approached by Australia earlier this year, but the Azzurri's failure to qualify for the World Cup seemingly resulted in a change of heart, and he pledged for the Socceroos.

Sports.title: Aston Villa in talks to sign another Chelsea outcast after Alejandro Garnacho - as Maxence Lacroix undergoes Blues medical ahead of £55m move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Lacroix closes in on £55m Chelsea move

Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today after the Blues agreed a deal for the Crystal Palace defender worth around £55m on Thursday.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this week, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish, who were in New York for the World Cup final, met at the Aman Hotel near Central Park on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Chelsea had revisited their interest in the 26-year-old early this summer.

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Crystal Palace and France star Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today

Villa in talks to sign Jackson

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson.

The clubs have already agreed a loan with obligation deal for Alejandro Garnacho to join Villa. That followed the £117m sale of Morgan Rogers.

The structure of the deals are key as Chelsea and Villa are among those that need to comply with Uefa's squad cost ratio regulations and their 2025 settlement agreements.

Rogers' £117m move will provide Villa with a significant accounting profit, potentially over £80m after Middlesbrough's sell-on clause and the remaining book value of his 2024 signing are deducted.

But if Chelsea had sold Garnacho to Villa as part of the same transaction, Uefa would treat it as a swap deal, impinging on profit margin. Even if Garnacho left on deadline day September 1, that is fewer than the guideline of 45 days, making it harder to argue they are not connected.

A loan with an obligation to buy could still be regarded as part of a swap deal because the 'purchase' has been agreed within 45 days of Rogers' transfer but the conditions give Villa control of when that deal is completed and potential room for manoeuvre with Uefa regulators.

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson

Summerville's Saudi switch confirmed

Al-Hilal have confirmed the signing of winger Crysencio Summerville from West Ham in a deal worth up to £60million.

The 24-year-old, who also had an offer from Roma, had a medical in Amsterdam on Tuesday.

Al Hilal will pay an initial fee of £55m, plus £5m in potential add-ons.

Magpies get their man

Aladji Bamba will wear the number eight shirt vacated by Sandro Tonali, after completing his £30million move to Newcastle United.

Bamba arrived from Monaco on Thursday and Newcastle will pay a further £5.5m in add-ons.

The 20-year-old has signed a five-year contract and manager Eddie Howe said: 'He's another exciting, young signing who we're really looking forward to working with.

'Aladji adds depth and a range of qualities to our midfield options, with a huge potential for growth.

'His development since breaking through at Monaco has been really impressive and something we believe we can help him build on.

'He operates in a deeper role but has the ability to contribute all over the pitch, which he demonstrated in both Ligue Un and the Champions League last season.'

Meanwhile, Newcastle say they have still to receive a formal offer from Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes.

No Blues interest in Bruno

Chelsea are not expected to pursue a move for Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

There had been suggestions that the West London club were interested in the Brazilian international, but Chelsea sources categorically refute this.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Chelsea have not, at any point, enquired about Guimaraes and sources maintain they have no plans to.

BOBBY MANZI

Ex-Burnley star catching Tigers' interest

Hull City are interested in Burnley midfielder Florentino Luis.

The Portuguese was on loan from Benfica last season, but Burnley have just made that move permanent for £20million as their obligation from the original deal.

However, Burnley are also understood to be willing to sell the 26-year-old to recoup funds and salary while they are in the Championship.

Boro target World Cup star

Middlesbrough are in talks to sign USA midfielder Sebastian Berhalter from Vancouver Whitecaps.

Boro are paying £900,000 for the 25-year-old who has 18 caps and played in all of the USA's World Cup games.

The deal includes a further £600,000 in add-ons.

Berhalter was born in London where his father Gregg, a former USA coach, was a player at Crystal Palace.

Boro remain in talks for left-back Max Arfsten from Columbus Crew also.

Middlesbrough are in talks to sign USA star Sebastian Berhalter from Vancouver Whitecaps
